## v0.2 role

Extract only the deterministic decision vocabulary shared by the three ratified managed adapters: ModelDemand, RouteObservation, EvidenceProvenance, AccountLease, BrokerDecision, ProxyAttempt, and typed failures. The core must be pure/clock-injected and property-testable.

* Synchronization belongs around shared mutable lease/session views, not inside pure reducers.

* Claude and Codex adapters consume the same pure election/failure types.
* OpenCode conformance can implement the process contract without provider-specific branches in the core.
* Seeded properties cover determinism, exact-model preservation, one-alternate budget, asymmetric staleness, and no-starvation tie-breaking.
* Remote check passes.

issues.title: Managed provider re-enrollment transaction clears hard refresh quarantine
issues.description:
## Outcome

A route in `hard_lineage_invalidated` can return to service only through one managed, provider-owned re-enrollment transaction that proves a newly issued credential lineage and durably resolves both hard authorities. Raw provider login by itself is not clearance.

## Contract

* Acquire the existing per-provider/account flock and the exact upstream-identity flock when available.
* Snapshot only redacted pre-enrollment generation/fingerprint evidence in memory; never persist tokens or provider response bodies.
* Launch the provider-owned login in the account's isolated config/browser boundary.
* Re-read the canonical credential under the same transaction and prove a fresh usable access token plus refresh token and a new credential generation. Same identity is allowed; stale or unchanged rotating-token lineage is not.
* Commit a closed `provider_reenroll_resolved` event and marker transition with crash ordering that never exposes a route between marker removal and durable resolution.
* Update the hard-lineage reducer so only that privately constructed resolution proof can clear the prior hard event. Ordinary `refreshed` rows, manual file edits, stale backups, and raw login success remain unable to clear it.
* On any ambiguity or partial persistence, preserve hard quarantine and emit a redacted typed failure.
* Claude/Codex enrollment remains provider-owned; browser isolation follows TIN-2071. Setup/repair presentation follows TIN-3006.

## Acceptance

* Fake-provider tests cover success, unchanged token lineage, identity drift, canceled login, torn credential, lock contention, crash points on both sides of the durable resolution commit, and restart reduction.
* Tests prove stale backup restoration and ordinary refresh/login rows cannot clear hard state.
* Status/doctor expose whether managed clearance is available and the exact safe next action without implying an unavailable flow.
* Exact-head GF test/check, required CI, and Public Source pass.
* No live provider call or installed/service mutation is required for code acceptance; attended provider proof is a later promotion gate.

## Claim boundary

This is recovery plumbing, not managed continuity proof. TIN-2057 remains unchanged until a separately authorized attended handoff/repair gate passes.

issues.title: Managed sidecars: 256-bit per-session capability on every loopback request
issues.description:
## Risk

A loopback token-attaching proxy without client authentication is a credential oracle to other local processes.

## Contract

* Generate 256 random bits from Zig std crypto RNG and base64url encode them into `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` for the managed Claude child.
* Store the capability in session memory only; never persist or log it.
* Validate the inbound bearer in constant time on every request, then strip all inbound auth/API-key headers.
* Missing/wrong capability returns a typed local 401 and performs zero DNS, connect, or upstream I/O.
* Revoke on child exit/sidecar teardown. Distinct sessions cannot reuse capabilities.
* A feasibility test must first prove Claude Code carries `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` as the expected bearer through `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`.

## Threat boundary

This protects against accidental/opportunistic same-user localhost calls, not root, a same-user debugger, or a fully compromised host. TLS on loopback and multi-tenant hosting are out of scope.

## Acceptance

Unit tests cover generation/encoding/constant-time comparison and redaction. Fake-upstream process tests prove bad-token zero-call behavior, cross-session rejection, teardown revocation, and no capability in logs/crash artifacts.

issues.title: Health-key codec: reject separator collisions and overflow at config validation
issues.description:
## Problem

TIN-3006 review found a broader pre-existing invariant gap outside its three-file charter.

`src/health.zig` encodes route state into a fixed 256-byte `provider:account#capability` key. `KeyBuf.append` silently truncates, and `parseHealthKey` interprets the first `#` after the provider/account separator as the capability boundary. Current config validation rejects `:` in provider names but does not reject `#` in account/capability names or prove that every configured account/capability key fits losslessly.

That permits two configured routes to collide or become unparseable in persisted health state. TIN-3006 fails closed at its new planning front doors, but it must not expand into shared config/health ownership.

## Scope

* Define one lossless health-key constructor/validator shared by config and runtime users.
* Reject reserved separators in account and capability names at config validation.
* Reject any configured account or capability route whose encoded key exceeds the codec limit; do not truncate.
* Cover custom provider definitions as well as built-ins.
* Preserve valid colon-containing account labels if the codec/parser contract intentionally supports them.
* Audit all direct `accountKey`/`capabilityKey` callers for silent-truncation assumptions.

## Acceptance

* Config validation fails with field-specific errors for `#` collisions and overlong account/capability routes.
* Property/boundary tests prove encode/parse round-trip and uniqueness for all accepted keys.
* No runtime health path can create a truncated key.
* Existing valid config and emitted compatibility bytes remain unchanged.
* Exact-head GF Test and GF Check pass.

## Claim boundary

This is route-state integrity hardening. It does not move Stage 4, G11, or TIN-2057 and does not authorize credential/provider access.

issues.title: Flock unlink-on-release race: two processes can hold the same account/identity lock
issues.description:
**Public surface: GH #373** — close both together.

`RepairLock.release()` closes the fd (`src/repair_state.zig:63`) then unlinks the path (`:65`): a blocked waiter acquires on the old inode, the unlink orphans it, a later acquirer creates a new inode at the same path → **two holders of the same** `provider:account` **/ identity lock** → concurrent same-account sessions → refresh-chain self-revocation. Secondary trigger: macOS lock dir is `/tmp/oauth-mux-<uid>` (`src/paths.zig:24-38`); periodic /tmp cleaning unlinks held locks.

**In scope**

* Remove unlink-on-release (or unlink-before-close while locked); keep lock files persistent.
* Relocate macOS lock dir off /tmp.
* Two-process regression test: release-while-waiter-blocked asserts single ownership.

**Out of scope**: broker-owned CredentialLock redesign (that is the epic's larger arc); lock-wait UX (separate ticket).

**Acceptance**: test demonstrates the old code fails and new code holds; canary unaffected; no lock files deleted at session end.

This must land before the TIN-1852 gate is considered meaningful — the gate's "no leftover lock holders" condition is currently checkable only because the bug *deletes* the evidence.

issues.title: Claude managed adapter: authenticated per-session ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL request proxy
issues.description:
## Outcome

Implement the v0.2 managed Claude adapter as a per-session authenticated loopback request proxy. `omux claude [-- <args>]` launches Claude Code with an ephemeral `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and a base64url 256-bit capability in `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`. Bare `claude` is untouched.

## Contract

* Bind loopback only; keep the capability memory-only, compare in constant time, strip it upstream, and return local 401 with zero upstream calls on mismatch. An instrumented launch must prove Claude Code's bearer carrier before claiming this boundary.
* Forward origin-form requests only to compile-fixed `https://api.anthropic.com`; reject CONNECT, absolute-form, arbitrary destinations, caller-selected upstreams, and credential-carrying redirects.
* Strip inbound auth/API-key headers and inject only the elected account's OAuth credential.
* Preserve the exact requested model.
* Permit one cross-account alternate only for explicit pre-body 401/403/429. Provider 5xx passes through. Never replay started responses or ambiguous transport outcomes.
* Replay budgets are 32 MiB/request, 64 MiB/sidecar, and 256 MiB/host with atomic reservations/stale-PID cleanup. Budget or chunked overflow becomes stream-once; no disk spooling.
* Refresh at request boundary through the existing per-account flock. Hard rotating-refresh-token failure quarantines the route and requires provider-owned re-enrollment; never restore stale token backups.
* When all routes are exhausted, wait once only for a trusted reset within 30 seconds and the request deadline, then typed 429 plus Retry-After.
* The resident service remains refresh/observation/alert/snapshot only, never the request proxy.

## First proof

A deterministic fake Anthropic upstream proves carrier behavior, bad-token zero-call rejection, fixed-origin/redirect negatives, streaming pass-through, exact-model preservation, single-alternate 401/403/429, 5xx pass-through, ambiguous/started exclusions, replay budgets, cleanup, and redaction. Live proof follows under TIN-2077.

issues.title: Exact-model Claude route readiness across N accounts: evidence, staleness, and leases
issues.description:
## v0.2 role

Provide exact-model route readiness for the managed Claude broker across N enrolled accounts. Credentials remain account-scoped; there is no per-model credential refresh. Model demand comes from the request body's exact `model` value and must not be silently downgraded.

## Evidence and confidence

* Live traffic headers are highest-confidence observations. The committed Anthropic unified 5-hour/7-day header fixture is account-level unless evidence proves a narrower scope.
* `GET /api/oauth/usage` is an undocumented default advisory input only. Parse tolerantly with required-field checks, cache briefly, attach provenance/freshness, and disable only this source on schema drift.
* Known exhausted-with-reset remains trusted until reset. Known available expires on a freshness deadline. Unknown is eligible for reactive proof but ranks below known-good and above dead/quarantined.
* Missing observations never manufacture model parity or capacity; the broker falls back to reactive request-boundary classification.

## Routing contract

Fold observations into the existing `provider:account#capability` health key and pure quota bucket core. Exact-model eligible routes are selected with sticky least-loaded session leases and identity-family collapse. Shared cross-process lease state must be bounded, redacted, stale-PID recoverable, and advisory rather than a credential authority.

## Acceptance

1. The Claude proxy extracts and preserves the exact model on every attempt.
2. Two accounts can carry different evidence/freshness for the same model without conflating credential health.
3. Unknown/known-good/exhausted/dead ordering and asymmetric staleness are property-tested with injected time.
4. Advisory usage schema drift degrades to reactive routing without ending the session.
5. Concurrent sidecars share lease pressure without starvation at 20 sessions/50 accounts.
6. Committed evidence clearly distinguishes provider-observed model data from account-level inference.

issues.title: Claude proxy product gate: strict performance, bounded replay memory, and concurrency
issues.description:
## Outcome

Gate the managed Claude proxy on measured product performance and exact-once correctness, not micro-optimization claims.

## Required budgets

* Local routing/auth overhead before upstream I/O: p95 <= 5 ms, p99 <= 10 ms.
* Sustained SSE throughput: within 5% of direct Claude Code.
* Idle sidecar RSS: <= 20 MiB.
* No starvation at 20 concurrent managed sessions across 50 enrolled accounts.
* Replay memory: 32 MiB/request, 64 MiB/sidecar, 256 MiB/host. Use atomic cross-process reservations with stale-PID cleanup.
* Missing reservation or chunked/unknown-length overflow degrades to stream-once with backpressure; never disk spool.

## Correctness

At most two upstream attempts. Only explicit pre-body 401/403/429 can select one alternate. Provider 5xx passes through. Ambiguous transport, cancellation, partial writes, and started responses never cross accounts. Health/state writes must be atomic and state-change-bounded.

Persistent HTTP clients, buffered header parsing, and parse/write deduplication are implementation tools only when measurement justifies them; do not buffer successful SSE bodies.

## Acceptance

A deterministic fake Anthropic upstream plus a direct-vs-proxy benchmark publishes redacted artifacts for latency percentiles, throughput, RSS, memory-pressure fallback, stale reservation cleanup, attempt counts, and 20x50 lock fairness. This blocks TIN-2057.

issues.title: Bounded request-boundary lock wait and one-alternate re-election
issues.description:
## Problem

Request-boundary refresh/materialization can block indefinitely on a sibling session's per-account flock and make the managed harness appear hung.

## Contract

* Use the existing announced per-account flock shared with resident keepalive.
* Bound lock acquisition by the remaining request deadline; never wait indefinitely.
* A locked candidate is unavailable for that election round and may cause re-election only within the request's single cross-account alternate budget.
* Never select a third account or retry an ambiguous/started request.
* Emit a typed redacted lock-wait/skip event.
* If no route is selectable, apply the program's all-exhausted rule: one wait only for a trusted reset within 30 seconds and the request deadline, then typed 429 plus Retry-After.

## Acceptance

Synthetic concurrent-process tests hold the first and alternate locks, prove bounded completion, attempts <=2, no deadlock with resident refresh, and either success on the sole eligible alternate or a classified terminal result.

issues.title: Shared cross-process Claude lease view with stale-owner recovery
issues.description:
## Purpose

Close the two lease predicates that the pure in-process [TIN-1790](https://linear.app/tinyland/issue/TIN-1790/extract-pure-broker-decision-core-for-claude-codex-and-opencode) state machine intentionally cannot prove: deterministic shared leases across concurrent per-session sidecars and safe stale-owner cleanup.

## Contract

* Persist only a redacted advisory lease view under the platform runtime/state directory; never store credentials, request bodies, provider payloads, raw account IDs, emails, or browser data.
* Serialize readers/writers with the repo's announced bounded flock pattern.
* Identify owners with PID plus process-incarnation/start evidence and heartbeat/generation so PID reuse cannot inherit a lease.
* Use atomic replacement and bounded recovery after crash or partial write.
* Treat missing, malformed, locked, or unavailable lease state as advisory unavailable: preserve reactive routing and never invent capacity or credential authority.
* Keep session stickiness and load pressure deterministic across sidecars; stale owners contribute neither load nor stickiness.

## Acceptance

1. Two real processes contend on one lease view without lost updates, corruption, or unbounded wait.
2. Crash and stale-owner scenarios reclaim safely; a reused PID cannot claim the predecessor's lease.
3. Concurrent sidecars observe shared pressure and deterministic selection; `deterministic_shared_leases` and `stale_lease_owner_cleanup` move only from wire-observed Stage 2 facts.
4. Artifact/event/canary scans prove the view is value-free.
5. Cross-process tests run remotely with no provider calls, credential reads, installation, or service mutation.
6. [TIN-2040](https://linear.app/tinyland/issue/TIN-2040/claude-proxy-product-gate-strict-performance-bounded-replay-memory-and)'s 20-session/50-account fairness benchmark consumes this representation but remains a separate G4 measurement.

issues.title: keepalive: integer-overflow panic in KeepaliveWait.wait on far-future (never=maxInt) wake sentinel
issues.description:
**Real runtime crash in the shipped** `oauth-mux keepalive` **command**, found live during the 2026-07-03 5-Claude Stage-2 dogfood soak (evidence: `docs/evidence/keepalive-warm-loop-20260703T171242Z/keepalive-soak-5x60s.stderr.log`).

## Symptom

`oauth-mux keepalive --iterations 5 --interval-ms 60000 --json` panicked:

```
thread ... panic: integer overflow
... in _main.KeepaliveWait.wait
```

## Root cause

`warm_scheduler.zig:57` defines `pub const never: i64 = std.math.maxInt(i64)` — the sentinel a not-due/idle account contributes to `nextWakeMs`. That far-future value flowed into `KeepaliveWait.wait` (`src/main.zig`), whose old arithmetic computed `wake_at_ms - now` (i64) and `sleep_ms * std.time.ns_per_ms` (u64) without total-function guards, so the sentinel path could overflow. Trips whenever the foreground loop sleeps against a `never` wake — i.e. a routine soak where accounts aren't due — so it is not an edge case, it is the common idle path.

## Fix (in-flight, uncommitted in the 2026-07-03 lab session working tree; Codex-authored)

Extracted `boundedKeepaliveSleepMs(wake_at_ms, now_ms, cap_ms) -> u64`: early-return on `wake ≤ now` or `cap == 0`; checked subtract (`std.math.sub(i64,…) catch maxInt`); clamp to `min(delta, cap, 24h)` **before** the ns multiply so neither the i64 subtract nor the u64 multiply can overflow. Pure + unit-tested ("keepalive wait sleep is bounded for far-future wake-up sentinels"). Independently verified SOUND (session 9925b2e2): total-function reasoning + empirical — the reran soak did 5 ticks clean (exit 0), `nix develop -c zig build test` green, `just remote-test` green (GF run 28674832621).

## Acceptance

* `boundedKeepaliveSleepMs` (or equivalent) lands on main with the far-future-sentinel unit test; a `keepalive --iterations N` soak over idle (not-due) accounts runs N ticks with no panic.
* Nit to fold in: add a unit case exercising the 24h `max_ms` clamp specifically (current far-future test hits the `cap` clamp first).

Blocks nothing shipped-critical (the fix is ready to land as its own PR, separate from the dogfood evidence docs). Surfaced by the 5-Claude credential-keepalive dogfood; noted in TIN-2057's Stage-2 comment. — filed session 9925b2e2, 2026-07-03; dup-checked (no existing ticket).

issues.title: P0 enabler: invert embedded clock in classification path → pure quota reducer (src/quota/bucket.zig)
issues.description:
**Parent: TIN-2400. The one July-safe, no-behavior-change increment of the model-quota-granularity design.** GH tracking: Jesssullivan/oauth-mux#436. Design of record: `docs/spec/model-quota-granularity-2026-07-03.md`.

## What

Two production sites read `std.time.timestamp()` *inside* the classification/observation path, which makes the fold impure and untestable:

* `recordHttpClassification` (health.zig:862)
* the `quota/observe` RPC handler `quotaObserve` (methods.zig:429)
  (and the selector `muxDecision` reads it at health.zig:949).

Invert them so **events carry** `at` and **queries take** `now`, exactly as `warm_scheduler.zig` already models its pure clock-injected core. Extract the pure quota algebra into a new `src/quota/bucket.zig`: `reduceBucket` (confidence-lattice LWW fold), `effectiveStatus(b, now)` (availability as a query), `deriveResetsAt` (non-optional reset instant), and the `BucketStatus`/`Evidence` sum types.

## Why

No behavior change — this is a shape enabler. It (a) makes the classification reducer property-testable (the 8 invariants in the design doc §3.7), and (b) ensures July credential-keepalive code adopts the `#capability` route key, `Evidence`/`confidence`, and event-`at` shapes so the August P1–P4 model-bucket work needs no rework. Safe to land during July because it touches no routing behavior and no provider wire.

## Acceptance

* `src/quota/bucket.zig` exists as a pure module (no clock/net/alloc import in the reducer/query fns; compile-time structural assertion).
* The two clock-read sites become event-`at`/query-`now`; `zig build test` green + the property tests pass.
* No change to any produced route decision or refresh timing (regression: warm-loop wakes bit-identical).

Category-error guard (carried from the parent): this is NOT per-model token refresh — credential is per-account; this only reshapes the observation/classification core. Does NOT block the July dogfood.

— filed by keepalive-push session 9925b2e2, 2026-07-03; dup-checked (no existing ticket for this refactor).

issues.title: claudeKeychainService default-dir contradiction: derivation always suffixes but ~/.claude should use the base service (TIN-2060 edge)
issues.description:
Surfaced by the TIN-2054-#2 review (confirmed latent, pre-existing — not introduced by the guard).

`provider_schema.claudeKeychainService` ALWAYS appends a `-<sha256(dir)[:8]>` suffix, yet its own doc-comment (and the TIN-2060 proof) states the default dir `~/.claude` uses the **unsuffixed base** `Claude Code-credentials` (the service bare Claude Code uses when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is unset). So:

* A managed Claude account configured with `config_dir: "~/.claude"` (or `$HOME/.claude`) and `service: null` derives `Claude Code-credentials-<hash(~/.claude)>` — the **wrong** service. The real item for that dir is (per the bare-CLI contract) the unsuffixed base, so oauth-mux would **read/write a non-existent/foreign keychain item** → the account is broken at the read layer before refresh ever runs.
* The TIN-2054-#2 canonical-keychain guard (exact-match on the unsuffixed base) therefore CANNOT catch this suffixed-but-wrong form. It only protects the literal base-string form (what `omux init` produces, and what the live `personal` account uses). The `~/.claude`-as-config_dir case is independently malfunctioning, so practical revoke-risk is low — but the comment-vs-code contradiction is a real latent defect.

**Root unknown (TIN-2060):** does the Claude CLI use the suffixed or the base service when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is exported AND equals the default `~/.claude`? Resolve it, then:

* **(a)** special-case `claudeKeychainService` to return the unsuffixed base when the absolute dir equals the resolved `~/.claude` (so the derived service matches the CLI's, and the canonical guard's exact-match correctly catches the only true bare-Claude form); OR
* **(b)** document that `~/.claude` is unsupported as a managed `config_dir` and refuse it at config-load (the cleaner posture, since a managed account should never share the bare-Claude item — and the live `personal` account, which IS `~/.claude`, should perhaps be modeled as "the user's own Claude, not mux-managed for refresh").

**Acceptance:** the derived keychain service for a `~/.claude` config_dir matches whatever the live CLI actually uses (golden-vector verified), OR `~/.claude` is explicitly refused as a managed config_dir with a clear message. Connects to TIN-2078 (declarable os-keystore).

issues.title: GOLDEN METRIC v0.2: one-click managed Claude + Codex continuity with model parity
issues.description:
## Product bar

An engineer installs the exact signed v0.2 candidate, enrolls operator-owned or organization-authorized accounts, and runs `omux <harness>`. When the active route exhausts eligible capacity, the same harness process preserves its context and exact requested model, uses one safe alternate, and completes without login, repair, relaunch, resume, or restart.

Repo authority: `docs/runbooks/omux-v0.2-evaluation-ladder-2026-07-14.md` and the v0.2 program linked from GitHub #463.

## Current score

**0/11 on current main** `c9dce4676481e9e7c64e96b2391f8f7332d8d419`**.** PR #521 merged signed candidate `b7f75c3ef1983ac07a468106c83c366abd0af722`; its merge tree exactly matches candidate tree `fb687a17328c7ac84e13bdb2c252f4b4e57096ed`. PR CI `31615091113` passed 9/9, Public Source `31615091160`, GF Test `31615102924`, and GF Check `31615114787` passed. Immutable Stage 2 run `31615220797` intentionally failed the incomplete 124-predicate gate while its downloaded artifact independently reconciled byte-for-byte to **82** **pass / 0 fail /** **42** **missing** from 113 value-free observations. Post-merge CI `31617244004` passed 9/9 and Public Source `31617243991` passed. G4 remains **0/6**. A golden row moves only from committed, redacted evidence for one exact candidate accepted on this issue.

## Golden rows

 1. **G1 Claude continuity:** one Claude process and context survive a provider-originated pre-body `quota_exhausted` 429 through exactly one distinct-identity `C1 -> C2` alternate with the exact model.
 2. **G2 replay memory safety:** ambiguity, partial send, cancellation, started response, 5xx, oversize, and exhausted budgets never cross identities or persist request bytes.
 3. **G3 exact-model readiness and leases:** exact-model evidence, asymmetric staleness, advisory kill-switch/reactive fallback, sticky least-loaded selection, and deterministic shared leases pass.
 4. **G4 performance:** the dedicated GF benchmark passes every pinned latency, throughput, memory, concurrency, and starvation predicate.
 5. **G5 managed boundary and redaction:** carrier, loopback, fixed origin, auth stripping, redirect/SSRF refusal, zero-call rejection, teardown, and allowlist-only evidence pass.
 6. **G6 resident independence:** resident absence or an allowed restart cannot make it the session proxy, expose request bodies, or corrupt the managed session.
 7. **G7 distribution and rollback:** signed macOS and Linux-beta install/upgrade, explicit unsupported Windows behavior, exact installed provenance, and rollback pass.
 8. **G8 Codex continuity:** one Codex process and context survive provider-originated exhaustion through exactly one distinct-identity `X1 -> X2` alternate with the exact model.
 9. **G9 OpenCode conformance:** OpenCode proves the surface-v2 lifecycle, route/lease vocabulary, bounded failure, redaction, compatibility, and explicit unsupported behavior.
10. **G10 bounded failure:** all-exhausted and resident-unavailable cases end once with a typed outcome and trusted `Retry-After`, without loops, invented capacity, or restart.
11. **G11 beta cohort:** three clean non-maintainer users, including one Linux user, complete install, enrollment, managed launch, handoff, repair, and rollback on the exact candidate.

## Trigger and claim boundary

The live G1/G8 trigger is provider-originated quota exhaustion. Pre-body 401/403 remain required synthetic negative coverage but do not substitute for the live continuity trigger. Stages 0-3 are prerequisites and earn no row. Stage 4 installed/service dogfood remains blocked until TIN-1759 is Done with accepted proof and the ladder's O-OWNERSHIP and R-TIN-1759 gates are accepted. v0.1.15 stays the stable shipped release until promotion is explicitly accepted.

issues.description:
## Outcome

Add defense-in-depth source containment for the omux macOS resident service before any v0.2 installed dogfood: launch the resident process under an exact empty-environment wrapper, keep service status value-free, and preserve doctor version/SHA truth.

This is a source-only precursor to TIN-1759. It cannot close TIN-1759 or open Stage 4; live launchd-domain remediation, controlled restart, proof, and rotate-last remain owned by the parent.

## Scope

* Render the LaunchAgent with exact argv `/usr/bin/env -i HOME=<validated> USER=<validated> PATH=<fixed> NO_COLOR=1 <omux> keepalive ...`; remove plist `EnvironmentVariables`.
* Validate rendered HOME, USER, and executable inputs; reject unresolved placeholders, XML/sed metacharacters, unknown assignments, and `=` in the executable path.
* Make unit-text verification require the exact isolated argv.
* Make Darwin service status discard raw `launchctl print` output and emit fixed loaded/unloaded fields only.
* Extend doctor plist parsing to recognize the exact `env -i` wrapper and return the wrapped omux executable while preserving v0.1 direct-plist compatibility.
* Add a synthetic containment smoke and narrowly correct service docs that currently conflate unit-text inspection with live process isolation.

## Acceptance

* Legacy direct plist and exact wrapped plist both resolve the resident omux binary.
* Missing `-i`, unknown assignments, unsafe values, and unresolved placeholders fail closed.
* A synthetic inherited secret sentinel is absent from the fake child; HOME, USER, fixed PATH, and NO_COLOR remain.
* Synthetic raw launchctl output containing a sentinel never reaches status output.
* Smoke proves no bootstrap, bootout, kickstart, install, uninstall, provider, credential, or service mutation occurs.
* Exact-head GF Test, GF Check, release proof, PR CI, and Public Source pass.

## Claim boundary

May claim source-level launch environment isolation, value-free service status, compatibility parsing, and synthetic regression coverage only. Must not claim TIN-1759 closure, live containment, installed provenance, resident independence, rollback, Stage 4, G5/G6/G7, or any TIN-2057 row. v0.1.15 remains stable.

issues.title: Executable v0.2 proof harness: immutable candidate dispatch, Stage 2 conformance, and G4 benchmark
issues.description:
## Outcome

Make the v0.2 evaluation ladder executable and exact-candidate-bound. Generic repository tests remain useful, but they cannot stand in for Stage 2 conformance or G4 performance proof.

## Scope

* Add a 40-hex `candidate_sha` input for v0.2 proof dispatch. Dispatch uses a frozen ref whose event `headSha == candidate_sha`; the workflow checks out that detached commit, asserts `HEAD == candidate_sha`, and emits allowlist provenance containing candidate SHA, tree, target, run ID, worker class, and local-fallback status.
* Keep ordinary branch/ref dispatch for generic development checks, but make every v0.2 evidence recipe fail closed without an immutable candidate SHA.
* Add repo-native recipes for:
  * `v02-stage1-local` (debug only);
  * `v02-stage2-conformance` (GF, deterministic fake upstream, synthetic credentials, provider egress denied, zero provider-call counters);
  * `v02-benchmark` (GF direct-vs-proxy latency/throughput/RSS/memory/concurrency gate owned with TIN-2040).
* Emit a machine-readable predicate manifest so one passing composition test cannot be mistaken for Stage 2 exit.
* Add an exact-candidate successor record; historical candidate records remain immutable.
* Public Source remains complementary and cannot replace GF. TIN-2105 remains parallel/nonblocking and no Zig REAPI claim follows without its forced remote-process artifact.

## Acceptance

* Mutable-ref movement between dispatch and checkout cannot change tested bytes.
* Workflow `headSha`, checked-out `HEAD`, candidate record, and emitted provenance agree.
* Stage 2 proves every ladder predicate or reports the exact missing set; provider calls remain structurally impossible.
* G4 benchmark publishes the budgets required by TIN-2040.
* Local runs are labeled `local_debug_only`.
* No provider call, installed binary, service mutation, Stage 4 dogfood, golden row, or release claim occurs.

Authority: TIN-2057, GitHub #463, `docs/runbooks/omux-v0.2-evaluation-ladder-2026-07-14.md`.

issues.title: Alerting channel: push notifications for reauth-needed and keepalive failures (today everything is pull-only)
issues.description:
Gap review verdict: alerting EXISTS NOWHERE — every surface is pull-only (`stay-afloat handoffs --json`, `daemon events`, exit-nonzero launch prints, the parked web UI boards with meta-refresh). The golden metric's step 5 (chain dies → user is *told*, then completes a mediated handoff) has no push path.

**In scope**

* Define the alert event set from existing typed records (reauth-needed/handoff-emitted, keepalive refresh-failure/backoff-exhausted, account dead/retired, quota-exhausted chronic) — no new detection, only delivery.
* Tier-1 channels: (a) terminal/desktop notification on the host (macOS `osascript`/notify-send class, via the daemon); (b) generic webhook POST (redacted payload: account label + state + next-action, never tokens/ids) — the webhook doubles as the integration point for external automations.
* Channel config in config.json (off by default); delivery is best-effort, never blocks the state machine; redaction-by-construction payloads.
* Build on the broker `events/subscribe` design (the one designed push channel, currently unimplemented) where it fits, but do not block on the full broker daemon.

**Out of scope**: the web UIs (#347/#356 own their surfaces), email/SMS, the usage-stats feed (separate ticket — different cadence and consumer).

**Acceptance**: kill a test account's chain → a desktop notification and a webhook POST fire within one daemon tick, payload redaction-verified; no alert spam on repeated ticks (dedup/cooldown).

issues.title: Lock-wait UX: silent indefinite block on second same-account launch + readiness mislabels live sessions
issues.description:
Second launch of the same account blocks **silently and indefinitely** inside `acquireRepairLockBlocking` (`src/adapters/codex/main.zig:1420`) — no message until acquired; last status frame is `auth_refresh_preflight`. A live session holds the lock for its entire duration, so the second launch reads as a hang. Related diagnostics lie: readiness surfaces report a live session as "repair in progress (started N hours ago)" (`src/runtime.zig:156-158`).

**In scope**

* Emit "waiting for account lock (held by pid/session since <ts>)" to stderr + a status frame *before* the blocking open; repeat periodically.
* Optional `--no-wait` fast-fail flag mirroring the identity lock's refusal.
* Distinguish session-hold from repair-hold in `routeReadiness` (label `session_active` vs `repair_in_progress`).

**Out of scope**: changing lock granularity or hold duration.

**Acceptance**: second same-account launch prints an actionable wait line within 1s; `accounts list` shows `session_active` for a held live session.

issues.title: E2: Anthropic quota-signal evidence fixture — committed test/evidence/quota-observation/ (TIN-2400 P1 gate)
issues.description:
## What

The DOR's P1 evidence gate (`docs/spec/model-quota-granularity-2026-07-03.md` §5), pulled to this week per operator-approved plan 2026-07-09: a live-captured, redacted, committed `test/evidence/quota-observation/` proving Anthropic's real quota signals — the precondition for ANY model-quota claim (AGENTS.md gate).

Entitlement note: the tier question was already resolved locally 2026-07-04 (uniform `default_claude_max_20x` across all 5 accounts). This fixture answers what only live capture can: real header names, model dimension, 429 shapes, and that the tier label actually serves Fable-class requests.

## Protocol (honest spend ladder)

1. No-spend channel first: invalid POST /v1/messages (max_tokens:0 / unknown model) per account — whether limiter headers appear on 4xx is itself a finding.
2. Primary: micro-spend `max_tokens:1` per (account × {fable, opus, cheapest}) with an explicit spend ledger in the README (single-digit tokens, operator-approved).
3. Riding CLI traffic: rejected (no proxy exists) — recorded so nobody reaches for mitm without a decision.

Mechanics: new `scripts/capture-claude-quota-headers.sh` (precedent: [capture-codex-wire.sh](<http://capture-codex-wire.sh>)); tokens read from SUFFIXED keychain services only, passed via curl header file, never argv. Operator present.

## Fixture + redaction

`test/evidence/quota-observation/claude-<UTCts>/` — headers/bodies per (account-hash × model × status), entitlement matrix, README with UTC stamps + spend ledger + gitleaks record. Keep header NAMES and numeric limit values verbatim; sha256_12hex org/request/account ids (TIN-1822 convention); strip authorization entirely. Code tweak: `src/fixture_redaction.zig` gains `test/evidence/` as a second walk root.

## Code increment after capture (all confidence=assumed until fixture says otherwise)

* Fix claude_def rate-limit header names (provider_schema.zig:805-808) FROM fixture.
* Declare opus/fable/sonnet/haiku CapabilityDefinitions (aliases = observed model ids; probe=null passive-only; proof_status → fixture path).
* Claude 429/403 FailureRules ONLY if fixture shows generic classifyHttp arms mis-handle; else record that finding.
* Fixture-literal classifyHttp table tests. Remote lanes green.

## Acceptance

Committed fixture proving (a) real header names + model-dimension presence/absence, (b) window-vs-burst 429 shapes or their documented absence, (c) live Fable-serve confirmation per account, (d) spend ledger. **Absence of a signal is a valid result** — it locks the advisor's `unobserved` rendering and keeps the claim gate closed. Claim boundary unchanged: credential keepalive ≠ model-quota keepalive.

issues.title: Consume the Zig-emitted release manifest across supported install lanes
issues.description:
## Authority

`build.zig.zon` is the single human-edited version source and the Zig release graph owns target/product semantics. It deterministically emits and checks `release-manifest.json`. Consumers do not own independent versions or target lists.

## In scope

* GitHub release assets and checksums/signing inputs.
* Curl installer.
* Binary-only Homebrew formula.
* deb/rpm metadata.
* Nix/source consumption.
* Compatibility `oauth-mux` link beside primary `omux`.
* Service assets, SBOM/provenance, build ID, adapter protocol versions, and supported-platform declarations.

## Excluded

npm remains retired. Do not add `.pkg`, `.dmg`, AppImage, or another unratified lane. Windows managed broker is unsupported; any retained v0.1.15 artifact is compatibility history until the manifest explicitly removes it.

## Acceptance

One `build.zig.zon` version change causes the Zig graph to regenerate/check every supported consumer with no hand-edited drift. Clean-source and installed-artifact proofs agree on version, hashes, signatures, SBOM, provenance, and support matrix.

issues.title: v0.2 FOSS readiness: contribution, security, privacy, support, and fork-proof policy
issues.description:
## Why

Market-ready FOSS requires a stranger to understand how to build, report vulnerabilities, contribute, verify releases, and know what data stays local. Today those promises are scattered across old roadmaps and package docs.

## Scope

* Add or truth current `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, support matrix, privacy/local-data statement, migration guide, issue/PR templates, and release verification instructions.
* Public command/support matrix: macOS GA target, Linux beta, Windows managed broker unsupported; v0.1.15 stable until the v0.2 golden gate.
* Document fork policy: untrusted fork PRs execute no credentialed/private CI; contributors run public local checks; a maintainer promotes a trusted commit/branch for GloriousFlywheel remote proof.
* Ensure source builds and prerelease verification need no private endpoints or secrets.
* Publish dependency/license, SBOM/provenance, signing, checksum, and vulnerability-reporting boundaries.
* Keep browser/cookie-picker evidence explicitly operator-assisted and exclude cookies, tokens, raw account ids/emails, and PII screenshots.

## Acceptance

1. A clean non-maintainer can build, test, install a signed prerelease, verify checksums/provenance, and file a safe report using only public docs.
2. Fork PR behavior is tested and cannot execute privileged GF/provider lanes.
3. Security policy names the local loopback sidecar threat boundary and private reporting path without promising unsupported response SLAs.
4. Privacy copy matches local-only telemetry and no prompt/body persistence.
5. Docs are linked from README and the release/migration runbooks and pass remote proof.

issues.title: Guided Claude enrollment: isolated provider-owned browser context per account
issues.description:
## Outcome

Make per-account browser isolation a guided `omux setup` enrollment property, not a background reauth engine or runtime broker dependency.

Live evidence from TIN-2060 showed that a second Claude account can inherit the first account's browser session and fail to reach fresh consent/code delivery. Each provider-owned login therefore opens in a fresh private or ephemeral browser context.

## Scope

* `omux setup` launches the provider-owned Claude login with an isolated browser context for each account.
* The launcher may open a browser and report redacted progress; it never reads browser cookies, captures credentials, or signs in silently.
* Browser/cookie-picker tools remain evidence and operator assistance only.
* Runtime continuity uses the TIN-1829 sidecar and never depends on a browser.
* No custom reauth-job or flow-composition product is revived.

## Acceptance

* Two consecutive account enrollments each reach a fresh provider-owned login/consent surface.
* The resulting accounts have distinct isolated config/keychain identities.
* Tests and redacted evidence contain no cookies, token bytes, raw emails, or screenshots with PII.
* The flow returns to `omux setup`, verifies identity/model signals, and records explicit consent before admission.

issues.description:
## Outcome

A clean user reaches a ready managed Claude/Codex fleet through one guided `omux setup` flow without insider topology knowledge or hand-edited JSON.

## Flow

1. Preflight platform, harness binaries, keychain/secret-tool, service support, PATH/version truth, and existing config.
2. Collect labeled operator-owned accounts and desired Claude/Codex harnesses.
3. Stage isolated per-account stores and launch provider-owned login, one isolated browser context per identity.
4. Verify redacted identity uniqueness, declared model demand, entitlement/signal provenance, and account health.
5. Ask separately for consent to proactive refresh and managed switching; default deny on ambiguity.
6. Install/enable the user refresh/observation service only after confirmation.
7. Run a bounded readiness proof and print precise `omux repair <label>` actions for failures.

## Boundaries

No cookie import as auth, no hidden browser automation, no credential pooling, no daemon-required request proxy, and no broad provider wizard. Agent-safe JSON plan mode must not prompt or read secrets.

## Acceptance

Three steps or fewer from clean install to staged logins/readiness; idempotent rerun; no hand-edited config; macOS live proof and Linux systemd/secret-tool beta proof; redacted clean-user evidence.

issues.title: Release discipline: evidence-bound cut cadence, CHANGELOG maintenance, CI tag-drift warning
issues.description:
## Problem

61 PRs sat unreleased between v0.1.13 (2026-06-12) and v0.1.14 (2026-07-04) with zero signal — every packaged install lane served a binary predating the `oauth-mux keepalive` command, and the operator's own stale binary panicked mid-dogfood. There was no cadence, no CHANGELOG, and nothing that warns when the release channel drifts from main.

## Shipped already (PR #441, the v0.1.14 cut)

`CHANGELOG.md` exists with the discipline stated in its header: **cuts are bound to committed** `docs/evidence/` **dirs; claims stop at that evidence; a cut is owed whenever a flagship evidence dir lands.**

## Remaining scope

1. **CI tag-drift warning**: a cheap job (or PR-comment bot step) that computes `commits-ahead` and `days-ahead` of main vs the latest `v*` tag and warns on PRs when either crosses a threshold (propose: 20 commits or 14 days). Warning, never a gate.
2. **Runbook update**: fold the cadence rule + CHANGELOG maintenance into `docs/release-runbook.md` (currently updated 2026-05-09, pre-dates all of this).
3. **CHANGELOG gate**: the release-proof lane checks the tag's version has a CHANGELOG entry (fail the cut, not PRs).

Cross-refs: TIN-2050 (SSOT-derived lane generation — owns the lanes themselves, not the cadence), TIN-1830 (running-binary version/SHA visibility acceptance), TIN-2409 (Done — the stale-binary panic history). Posture: distribution-not-hosted; nothing here phones home.

— filed by deliverable-shape review (verified SOUND_WITH_FIXES), operator-approved 2026-07-04, session 9925b2e2; dup-checked (no existing cadence/CHANGELOG ticket for omux).

issues.title: omux setup/repair planning-only front door with zero credential or provider access
issues.description:
## Outcome

Land the smallest source-only `omux setup` and `omux repair` planning surface that lets a clean user inspect what will be required before any credential, provider, install, or service mutation is authorized.

This is a bounded child of TIN-2063, not the complete setup wizard and not installed dogfood.

## Public shape

* `omux setup [--provider claude|codex] [--label <label>] [--json]`
* `omux repair <label|provider:label> [--json]`

Every output declares:

* `mutates=false`
* `reads_credential_material=false`
* `executes_provider_cli=false`
* `spends_provider_calls=false`
* `managed_claude_forwarding=compile_disabled`
* `claim_level=planning_only`

## Implementation boundary

* Add first-class setup parsing and repair-label parsing in `src/cli.zig`; preserve legacy `setup codex` compatibility.
* Add pure setup/repair plan renderers in `src/main.zig`, reusing config validation, enrollment-plan serialization, and existing repair classification without invoking repair execution.
* Use observation-only runtime inspection. Do not call writability probes that create/delete markers.
* Gather binary presence/version only with execution disabled.
* Do not call account-list paths that can read keychain-backed entitlements.
* Never invoke provider CLIs, login, setup/install scripts, service operations, `runRepairRun`, or provider endpoints.

## Acceptance

issues.title: oauth-mux CI: add PR-scoped concurrency group to end the sequential-merge tax
issues.description:
## Problem

`oauth-mux/.github/workflows/ci.yml` has **no** `concurrency:` **key** in any job (grep-confirmed, 2026-07-02). Every job pins `runs-on: tinyland-nix`, and the cross-compile matrix alone demands 6 concurrent runner slots (30-min GitHub job cap; the 20-min figure is the inner build timeout). With a shared `tinyland-nix` pool and no concurrency group, N simultaneous PRs oversubscribe the pool and jobs that cannot claim a slot before the cap are **CANCELLED (timed-out), not FAILED**.

This is distinct from the GF-REAPI-proof singleton eviction already fixed by TIN-1959 / TIN-2185 / TIN-1777 — those serialize the *proof* dispatch against the singleton `gf-reapi-cell`. This ticket is about oauth-mux's own PR CI (cross-compile + cache-first) starving itself under concurrent PRs.

## Impact

The "drain PRs sequentially, one PR's CI at a time" merge-train rule is a **procedural workaround for an absent** `concurrency:` **group**, not an intrinsic property of the substrate. It cost real wall-clock during the 2026-07-02 keepalive-push merge train (#425/#426/#427/#428 had to be merged strictly one at a time; a main-push run was observed cancelled mid-flight when three things overlapped).

## Scope

* Add `concurrency: { group: ci-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }` (or equivalent per-ref group) to `ci.yml`, scoped so PR events cancel superseded runs of the same ref but never cancel `main` push validation.
* Verify a force-push to a PR branch cancels the stale run instead of leaving both queued.
* Confirm it does not interact badly with the required-checks merge gate (a cancelled superseded run must not leave a required check stuck pending on the live head).

## Acceptance

* Two rapid pushes to one PR branch → only the latest run survives; the older is cancelled deterministically (not slot-starved).
* Concurrent distinct PRs no longer cancel each other's cross-compile jobs.
* Merge-train serialization is no longer required for correctness (still fine as a courtesy under capacity limits).

Surfaced by the push-plan remote-infra orientation (DELTA-3 / gap G1). Cheapest high-value CI fix in the infra map.

— filed by push-plan infra orientation 2026-07-02 (oauth-mux PR #428, repo @ 08a6c87)

issues.title: first-run e2e claude-enroll block is Linux-shaped: asserts file backend, red on macOS where enroll writes keychain
issues.description:
## Problem

`scripts/first-run-e2e.sh` (the `just check-local` lane) asserts, in the "confirmed enroll claude adds isolated config dir without login" block:

* `.providers.claude.accounts.work.secret.backend == "file"`
* `.providers.claude.accounts.work.secret.path | contains(".credentials.json")`

But on macOS, `oauth-mux enroll claude --confirm-enroll` writes `"secret": {"backend": "keychain"}` with **no path field** (empirically reproduced 2026-07-02 at main @ `47ec4b8`: `init --codex-max` → `enroll claude --account work --confirm-enroll` → stanza `{"priority":10,"config_dir":".../claude/work","secret":{"backend":"keychain"},"tags":["oauth","claude"]}`). Both clauses are false on Darwin → the jq exits 1 → `just check-local` **is red on every Mac at main**, while the Linux GloriousFlywheel runner passes it.

## Impact

1. Operators lose the local pre-push gate on macOS — check-local cannot go green.
2. It masks real failures: during the PR #431 CI red today this macOS failure was hit first locally and initially looked like the TIN-1822 branch's defect (the actual remote failure was the separate smoke-broker fixture issue, fixed in `1b07a7f`/`24c20cc`).

## Fix directions (pick one)

* **(a)** Platform-aware assertion: accept `backend == "keychain"` (and no path clause) on Darwin, `file` + `.credentials.json` on Linux — mirrors what enroll genuinely does per platform.
* **(b)** Make the e2e force the file backend explicitly (if/when enroll grows a `--secret-backend file` flag), keeping the assertion platform-invariant.
* Whichever lands, assert the Darwin keychain stanza's derived service naming consistently with TIN-2104's resolution (the `~/.claude` special case is that ticket, not this one).

Related: TIN-2070 (keychain backend), TIN-2104 (service derivation contradiction), TIN-815 (e2e harness origin).

— filed by keepalive-push session 9925b2e2, 2026-07-02, repro at main `47ec4b8` on Darwin 25.6.0

issues.title: `oauth-mux version --check`: opt-in, offline-default binary staleness compare
issues.description:
## What

An explicit, opt-in staleness check for the running binary — the user-invocable complement to TIN-1830's `doctor` surfacing:

1. **Offline default**: `oauth-mux version --check` compares the running `build_id`/`binary_sha256` (already emitted in `version --json`, build.zig:85-115) against **local install-lane metadata** (a version/SHA sidecar the installer, brew formula, and packages write at install time). Reports match / stale / unknown-provenance. Zero network.
2. **Explicit online mode only**: `version --check --online` may consult the GitHub Releases endpoint to report the latest published tag. Never implicit, never cached-and-auto, **never invoked from the daemon loop or any managed session path**.
3. Detects and reports PATH shadowing (multiple `oauth-mux` executables on `$PATH`) — same class as the live 2026-07-03 finding (`~/.nix-profile` shadowing `~/.local/bin`).

## Posture (binding)

No phone-home, no telemetry, no auto-update. Grep-verified today: the binary makes zero network calls outside provider OAuth flows — this feature must keep it that way by construction (network only under the explicit `--online` flag). Distribution-not-hosted framing intact.

## Why

Two live staleness traps in two days (stale v0.1.13 panic mid-dogfood; PATH shadow). TIN-1830 surfaces provenance in `doctor` for the service context; this ticket is the stranger-facing check. Not a dup of TIN-2409 (Done — that was the panic fix/history).

— filed by deliverable-shape review (verified), operator-approved 2026-07-04, session 9925b2e2; dup-checked.

issues.description:
## Problem

The local production build renders, but responsive/browser QA found concrete launch defects:

* At 390px viewport, the home page reports `documentElement.scrollWidth = 822` while `innerWidth = 390`.
* The main offender is the provider matrix table, which renders at \~1035px wide despite being inside an overflow wrapper. On mobile this creates horizontal document overflow.
* `pnpm run build` emits SvelteKit missing-id warnings because global section navigation anchors are present on `/agent-snippet` and `/style-guide/`, where the home-page section ids do not exist.
* `/style-guide/?guide=1` and `/agent-snippet` each showed 17 missing hash targets in a DOM check.

## Evidence from 2026-04-29

Commands run from `/Users/jess/git/omux.xoxd.ai`:

```sh
pnpm run build
pnpm exec serve build -l 4177
# Chrome Playwright local render at 1440x1200 and 390x1200
```

Build warning class:

* links to `/agent-snippet#hero`, `/agent-snippet#problem`, etc. have no matching ids on `/agent-snippet`
* links to `/style-guide/#hero`, `/style-guide/#problem`, etc. have no matching ids on `/style-guide/`

Measured DOM:

* home desktop: `scrollWidth = 1440`, ok
* home mobile: `scrollWidth = 822`, not ok
* agent snippet mobile: `scrollWidth = 390`, but missing nav targets = 17
* style guide desktop: missing nav targets = 17

## Acceptance

* Home page at 390px, 430px, 768px, and 1440px has no document-level horizontal overflow.
* Provider matrix either becomes a responsive card/list on mobile or is constrained so its scroll is local and does not widen the document.
* Global section nav is home-only, or section links use absolute `/#id` targets and do not create missing-id warnings on non-home pages.
* `pnpm run build` has no missing-id warnings.
* Add a lightweight Playwright/DOM regression test for document overflow and missing hash targets.

## Problem

The current `omux.xoxd.ai` implementation has real plumbing, but the public product surface does not yet meet the house launch bar. It reads as a plain stacked document/code dump rather than a polished devtool launch page.

* `package.json` pins Skeleton `4.15.2`, Svelte 5.55, Vite 8, Effect 3.21, Shiki 4.

* The style guide exists, but production components do not yet turn that design system into a polished launch surface.
* Current page copy over-exposes citations and source-line mechanics in user-facing sections; that belongs in docs/spec or a proof appendix, not the primary adoption funnel.

## Acceptance

* Rework the first viewport into a polished static-first devtool launch surface: name, literal value prop, install command, one high-signal live mux/probe visualization, and two clear CTAs.

* Import/adapt the proven house CSS patterns intentionally: font stack, code font treatment, sticky-header anchor offset, drawer transitions, section rhythm, and component utilities where appropriate.
* Keep Skeleton 4.15.2 and Tailwind 4; do not use this as an excuse to churn the stack.

issues.title: M4.1 DNS Cloudflare CNAME + Pages custom domain + TLS provisioning
issues.description:
## Why

Bring `https://omux.xoxd.ai` live. DNS via Cloudflare (NOT DreamHost — verified). Pages custom domain configured via API. TLS auto-provisioned by GitHub once DNS resolves.

## Scope

* Pre-flight: confirm Pages source is `actions`, repo Pages is enabled, `static/CNAME` content is `omux.xoxd.ai`, gitleaks clean, M3 content all merged
* Cloudflare DNS: add CNAME record `omux` → `tinyland-inc.github.io`, **gray-cloud (DNS-only)**, TTL 300
* Pages custom domain: `gh api -X PUT repos/tinyland-inc/omux.xoxd.ai/pages -f cname=omux.xoxd.ai` (do NOT set `https_enforced=true` until cert provisions)
* Verify: `dig +short omux.xoxd.ai` returns CNAME chain to `tinyland-inc.github.io` then `185.199.108-111.153`
* Wait for TLS provisioning (target 30 min, escalate at 1h, hard ticket at 24h)
* Once cert state is `approved`: `gh api -X PUT repos/tinyland-inc/omux.xoxd.ai/pages -F https_enforced=true`
* Add `oauth-mux.xoxd.ai` redirect via Cloudflare Redirect Rule (NOT multi-CNAME)

## Acceptance Criteria

* `curl -sI https://omux.xoxd.ai/` returns 200 with `server: GitHub.com`
* TLS cert state is `approved` with Let's Encrypt issuer
* `https_enforced: true` per Pages API
* HTTP redirects to HTTPS
* `oauth-mux.xoxd.ai` 301-redirects to `omux.xoxd.ai`
* ssllabs grade A or A+

issues.description:
## Why

The Nix dev shell + direnv loader + Justfile are the operator entrypoint for every dev workflow. Must land before package.json so contributors can `direnv allow && just setup` from a clean checkout.

## Scope

* `flake.nix` modeled on MassageIthaca shape: two inputs (`nixpkgs` unstable + `flake-utils`), single `devShells.default` providing `nodejs_22`, `nodePackages.pnpm`, `nodePackages.typescript`, `nodePackages.typescript-language-server`, `just`, `git`, `gh`, `bazelisk`, `gitleaks`. shellHook echoes versions.
* `.envrc` with `use flake` + `dotenv_if_exists .env .env.local` + `watch_file flake.nix flake.lock package.json`
* `Justfile` modeled on [jesssullivan.github.io](<http://jesssullivan.github.io>) (178 lines trimmed) with: `_default`, `setup`, `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `check`, `typecheck`, `lint`, `format`, `test-unit`, `test-e2e`, `test`, `ci`, `clean`, `clean-all`, `sync`, `analyze`, `regen-providers`, `info`, `gh-repo`. pnpm-driven.
* `flake.lock` committed after first lock

## Acceptance Criteria

* `direnv allow` enters shell with all tools present
* `just --list` shows the recipe set
* `just info` prints node 22 + pnpm 10.13.1 + just version
* `flake.lock` pinned and committed

initiativeBefore.summary: Six-week full-broker program: managed Claude proxy, Codex parity, exact-model failover, one-touch setup, FOSS delivery, and an authoritative subtractive reset.
initiativeBefore.description:
## Product bar

Install `omux`, enroll the operator's own accounts once, run `omux claude` or `omux codex`, and preserve the exact requested model across account exhaustion without restarting the harness or prompting for login at a safe request boundary.

## Five product projects

1. **Core + Subtraction** — pure broker types, v0.2 CLI/process contract, main.zig extraction, and deletion of superseded paths.
2. **Claude Managed Broker** — authenticated per-session `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` sidecar, fixed Anthropic origin, exact-model routing, one safe alternate, shared leases, and advisory quota observations.
3. **Adapter Contract + Codex/OpenCode Parity** — Codex remains the reference; OpenCode proves the versioned process/JSON-RPC contract generalizes.
4. **Delivery + FOSS** — `omux setup`, resident refresh/observation service, Zig-emitted release manifest, signed packages, contribution/security/privacy/support surfaces.
5. **Operator Trust + Evidence** — redacted local observability, rollout gates, weekly micro-spend compatibility, golden cohort, and prerelease promotion.

**External non-blocking workstream:** TIN-2105 owns pinned Bazel plus forced Zig/GF REAPI proof. It is related to this initiative, not a sixth product project and not a prerelease blocker.

## Binding decisions

* Managed launch only; bare harnesses remain unmanaged.
* Claude uses a per-session authenticated loopback request proxy to the compile-fixed Anthropic origin.
* Exact model by default; no silent model downgrade.
* One alternate only after explicit pre-body 401/403/429.
* Provider 5xx, ambiguous transport, and started responses never cross accounts.
* Replay caps: 32 MiB/request, 64 MiB/sidecar, 256 MiB/host; no disk spooling.
* An exhausted pool may wait once only for a trusted reset within 30 seconds and the request deadline; otherwise return typed 429 plus Retry-After.
* OAuth usage is advisory and provenance-carrying; reactive fallback remains.
* Local-only product; federation and hosted pooling are canceled.
* `build.zig.zon` and the Zig release graph emit/check the manifest consumed by packages and Bazel/GF.
* Rollout: shadow → manual-route → automatic beta → default managed.
* macOS GA target, Linux beta, Windows managed broker unsupported.
* Signed prereleases; v0.1.15 remains stable until the golden gate.
* Market gate: 2xClaude + 2xCodex, OpenCode conformance, and three clean non-maintainer installs including Linux.
* Performance gate: p95 <=5 ms, p99 <=10 ms, streaming within 5% of direct, idle RSS <=20 MiB, no starvation at 20 sessions/50 accounts.
* Untrusted fork PRs do not execute privileged GF CI; maintainer promotion to a trusted branch precedes authoritative proof.

## Authority

GitHub program: [https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/issues/463](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/issues/463>)

Repo authority packet: `docs/plans/oauth-mux-v0.2-full-broker-foss-program-2026-07-11.md`, `docs/security/omux-v0.2-threat-model-2026-07-11.md`, `docs/authority-map.md`, and the deletion ledger (phase-1 authority PR).

TIN-2057 remains the acceptance spine. Legacy narratives are completed, canceled, folded, or deleted after invariant migration rather than left as parallel authority.

## Charter

* Local-only trace IDs, bounded redacted event rings, statusline, doctor, and report.
* Transition notifications for successful switches and durable action-required states.
* Daily no-spend schema checks and weekly budgeted micro-spend adapter compatibility.

before.name: omux v0.2 · delivery + FOSS
before.summary: Deliver one guided setup, explicit user-service enablement, manifest-first packages, signed prereleases, and a credible public contributor/security surface.
before.description:
## Charter

* `omux` is primary; `oauth-mux` is the v0.2 compatibility link.
* `omux setup` owns guided enrollment, identity verification, scoped consent, and service enablement.
* Resident service owns refresh, observation, alerts, and redacted snapshots, not request proxying.
* Zig emits release-manifest.json; brew/curl/deb/rpm/Nix and Bazel/GF consume it.
* macOS GA target, Linux beta after secret-tool/systemd proof, Windows broker unsupported.
* Signed prereleases; v0.1.15 stays stable until the golden gate.
* CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, issue/PR templates, support matrix, privacy, migration, SBOM, and provenance.
* Public fork code is not executed; maintainers promote reviewed commits to trusted branches for GF proof.

Bazel/GF target-class promotion is parallel and non-blocking for prereleases.

before.name: oauth-mux Website Launch (omux.xoxd.ai)
before.summary: Public marketing/devtool website for oauth-mux at https://omux.xoxd.ai. Static-first SvelteKit on GitHub Pages, Skeleton 4.15.2 + real Bazel-registry consumer from M0.
before.description:
## Why

Build the public marketing and devtool surface for the oauth-mux FOSS project at `https://omux.xoxd.ai`. Repo lives at `tinyland-inc/omux.xoxd.ai`; canonical source at `Jesssullivan/oauth-mux` (now public, `v0.1.2` shipped).

This is the execution vehicle for the parent `TIN-734`. Its purpose per the founding prompt: align the Tinyland toolchain (Bazel module-catalog consumer, Nix flake, Justfile, Skeleton UI 4.15.2, Effect.ts, Vite 8 native) on a static-first SvelteKit application with room to expand to dynamic SaaS later.

## Scope

Deliver M-1 through M5 milestones over \~5 weeks targeting `2026-06-05`:

* **M-1** — Project management bootstrap (Linear + GitHub Project v2 + labels/templates + Bazel module catalog audit + [AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md](<http://AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md>) before implementation)
* **M0** — Repo and toolchain bootstrap (flake.nix, Justfile, MODULE.bazel + at least one low-risk catalog dep, package.json, dotfiles, vite/svelte config, app shell)
* **M1** — Toolchain hardening and CI (deploy-pages.yml, ci.yml, dependabot, branch protection via API, LICENSE)
* **M2** — Design system and theme (Skeleton 4.15.2 wired, Warm/Pragmatic OKLCH theme, ThemeSwitcher, layout, style guide page)
* **M3** — Content and IA (hero, problem, fallback algebra, install, first-run, security, provider matrix, contribute, contact — all backed by file_path:line citations into oauth-mux source)
* **M4** — First-viewport launch (DNS Cloudflare CNAME, Pages custom domain via API, TLS provisioning, repo flip to public, README rewrite)
* **M5** — Dynamic-ready scaffolding (provider matrix API, agent-snippet page, growth-path documentation)

## Acceptance Criteria

* Spec doc `docs/spec/omux-website-bootstrap-2026-04-29.md` is committed and reviewed
* Linear project + milestones + \~18-24 hybrid-granularity tickets exist and link to [TIN-734](https://linear.app/tinyland/issue/TIN-734/publish-oauth-mux-website-and-launch-narrative)
* GitHub Project v2 board exists for the public contributor surface
* [AGENTS.md](<http://AGENTS.md>) + [CLAUDE.md](<http://CLAUDE.md>) committed before implementation tickets start
* Skeleton 4.15.2 exact pin preserved through M0-M4 (v5 is post-launch watch only)
* `https://omux.xoxd.ai` is live by M4 with valid TLS
* "What not to claim" guardrails from oauth-mux planning doc honored in all copy

## Stack Baseline

Skeleton UI 4.15.2 exact, Svelte 5.55+, SvelteKit 2.58+, Vite 8 native (verify rolldown default), Effect 3.21.x, TypeScript 5.9.3 exact, pnpm 10.13.1 exact, Node 22, Bazel 8.2.1, Tailwind 4.2.x. `@tummycrypt/vite-plugin-skeleton-colors` + `skeletonTailwindV4Compat` shim per house v4 pattern. GitHub Pages with custom domain via Cloudflare gray-cloud DNS.

Planning doc: `docs/spec/omux-website-bootstrap-2026-04-29.md` in `tinyland-inc/omux.xoxd.ai`. M-1 PR open at [https://github.com/tinyland-inc/omux.xoxd.ai/pull/1](<https://github.com/tinyland-inc/omux.xoxd.ai/pull/1>).

milestones.name: M-1 Project Management Bootstrap
milestones.description: Establish exhaustive tracking surfaces before implementation churn. Linear project + milestones + tickets, GitHub Project v2, labels, templates, Bazel module catalog audit, [AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md](<http://AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md>). No DNS/Pages/dependency/scaffold mutation until this is in place. Spec doc must be committed first.

milestones.name: M0 Repo And Toolchain Bootstrap
milestones.description: flake.nix + .envrc + Justfile, package.json with all version pins (Skeleton 4.15.2, Vite 8 native, Effect 3.21.x, pnpm 10.13.1, Node 22, TS 5.9.3), MODULE.bazel + .bazelrc with at least one low-risk catalog dep, dotfiles, vite/svelte config, app shell, just check green.

milestones.name: M1 Toolchain Hardening And CI
milestones.description: CI workflow (lint + check + unit + build + e2e via Playwright), deploy-pages.yml (build + deploy gated to push-to-main), dependabot.yml, LICENSE, branch protection on main via API readback. ci-templates actions for nix-setup and secrets-scan where applicable.

milestones.name: M2 Design System And Theme
milestones.description: Skeleton 4.15.2 wired with skeletonTailwindV4Compat shim + tummycrypt vite-plugin-skeleton-colors. omux.css Warm/Pragmatic OKLCH theme (Skeleton 4 house format). Theme store + ThemeSwitcher. Layout (AppBar + Navigation + Dialog mobile drawer + footer). Style guide page at /style-guide?guide=1 with Skeleton 4 component smoke.

milestones.name: M3 Content And IA
milestones.description: All 9 sections per oauth-mux/docs/spec/product-adoption-sprint-2026-04-28.md authored: hero, problem, fallback algebra, install, first-run, security, provider matrix, contribute, contact. Content backed by file_path:line citations. Real CLI/JSON embedded from oauth-mux dist/live-qa. v0.1.3 commands (doctor, report, providers list) marked staged until merged. Sitemap + SEO + JSON-LD.

milestones.name: M4 First-Viewport Launch
milestones.description: DNS Cloudflare CNAME omux → [tinyland-inc.github.io](<http://tinyland-inc.github.io>) (gray-cloud, TTL 300). Pages custom domain configured via gh api. TLS provisions (target 30 min, escalate at 1h, hard ticket at 24h). Repo flips public. README rewritten. oauth-mux README cross-link PR. Soft-launch posts drafted. Live QA pass + Lighthouse all-green.

milestones.name: M5 Dynamic-Ready Scaffolding
milestones.description: Provider matrix as a JSON API endpoint. Agent-snippet page (copy-into-AI snippet). Optional changelog page from oauth-mux GitHub releases. Documented growth path (adapter-vercel/adapter-node escape hatch). Observability shape stub (analytics schema documented, none shipped at default). Skeleton v5 upgrade watch-only ticket placeholder.

before.name: omux v0.2: Full Broker FOSS Beta
before.summary: Six-week full-broker program: managed Claude proxy, Codex parity, exact-model failover, one-touch setup, FOSS delivery, and an authoritative subtractive reset.
before.description:
## Product bar

Install `omux`, enroll the operator's own accounts once, run `omux claude` or `omux codex`, and preserve the exact requested model across account exhaustion without restarting the harness or prompting for login at a safe request boundary.

## Five product projects

1. **Core + Subtraction** — pure broker types, v0.2 CLI/process contract, main.zig extraction, and deletion of superseded paths.
2. **Claude Managed Broker** — authenticated per-session `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` sidecar, fixed Anthropic origin, exact-model routing, one safe alternate, shared leases, and advisory quota observations.
3. **Adapter Contract + Codex/OpenCode Parity** — Codex remains the reference; OpenCode proves the versioned process/JSON-RPC contract generalizes.
4. **Delivery + FOSS** — `omux setup`, resident refresh/observation service, Zig-emitted release manifest, signed packages, contribution/security/privacy/support surfaces.
5. **Operator Trust + Evidence** — redacted local observability, rollout gates, weekly micro-spend compatibility, golden cohort, and prerelease promotion.

**External non-blocking workstream:** TIN-2105 owns pinned Bazel plus forced Zig/GF REAPI proof. It is related to this initiative, not a sixth product project and not a prerelease blocker.

## Binding decisions

* Managed launch only; bare harnesses remain unmanaged.
* Claude uses a per-session authenticated loopback request proxy to the compile-fixed Anthropic origin.
* Exact model by default; no silent model downgrade.
* One alternate only after explicit pre-body 401/403/429.
* Provider 5xx, ambiguous transport, and started responses never cross accounts.
* Replay caps: 32 MiB/request, 64 MiB/sidecar, 256 MiB/host; no disk spooling.
* An exhausted pool may wait once only for a trusted reset within 30 seconds and the request deadline; otherwise return typed 429 plus Retry-After.
* OAuth usage is advisory and provenance-carrying; reactive fallback remains.
* Local-only product; federation and hosted pooling are canceled.
* `build.zig.zon` and the Zig release graph emit/check the manifest consumed by packages and Bazel/GF.
* Rollout: shadow → manual-route → automatic beta → default managed.
* macOS GA target, Linux beta, Windows managed broker unsupported.
* Signed prereleases; v0.1.15 remains stable until the golden gate.
* Market gate: 2xClaude + 2xCodex, OpenCode conformance, and three clean non-maintainer installs including Linux.
* Performance gate: p95 <=5 ms, p99 <=10 ms, streaming within 5% of direct, idle RSS <=20 MiB, no starvation at 20 sessions/50 accounts.
* Untrusted fork PRs do not execute privileged GF CI; maintainer promotion to a trusted branch precedes authoritative proof.

## Authority

GitHub program: [https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/issues/463](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/issues/463>)

Repo authority packet: `docs/plans/oauth-mux-v0.2-full-broker-foss-program-2026-07-11.md`, `docs/security/omux-v0.2-threat-model-2026-07-11.md`, `docs/authority-map.md`, and the deletion ledger (phase-1 authority PR).

TIN-2057 remains the acceptance spine. Legacy narratives are completed, canceled, folded, or deleted after invariant migration rather than left as parallel authority.

requested.description:
## Native reset action

Remove adapter.acquire session-ID fallback for native request authority; require validated unique request ID and immutable demand/binding per attempt. before.title: Managed provider re-enrollment transaction clears hard refresh quarantine
before.description:
## Outcome

A route in `hard_lineage_invalidated` can return to service only through one managed, provider-owned re-enrollment transaction that proves a newly issued credential lineage and durably resolves both hard authorities. Raw provider login by itself is not clearance.

## Contract

* Acquire the existing per-provider/account flock and the exact upstream-identity flock when available.
* Snapshot only redacted pre-enrollment generation/fingerprint evidence in memory; never persist tokens or provider response bodies.
* Launch the provider-owned login in the account's isolated config/browser boundary.
* Re-read the canonical credential under the same transaction and prove a fresh usable access token plus refresh token and a new credential generation. Same identity is allowed; stale or unchanged rotating-token lineage is not.
* Commit a closed `provider_reenroll_resolved` event and marker transition with crash ordering that never exposes a route between marker removal and durable resolution.
* Update the hard-lineage reducer so only that privately constructed resolution proof can clear the prior hard event. Ordinary `refreshed` rows, manual file edits, stale backups, and raw login success remain unable to clear it.
* On any ambiguity or partial persistence, preserve hard quarantine and emit a redacted typed failure.
* Claude/Codex enrollment remains provider-owned; browser isolation follows TIN-2071. Setup/repair presentation follows TIN-3006.

## Acceptance

* Fake-provider tests cover success, unchanged token lineage, identity drift, canceled login, torn credential, lock contention, crash points on both sides of the durable resolution commit, and restart reduction.
* Tests prove stale backup restoration and ordinary refresh/login rows cannot clear hard state.
* Status/doctor expose whether managed clearance is available and the exact safe next action without implying an unavailable flow.
* Exact-head GF test/check, required CI, and Public Source pass.
* No live provider call or installed/service mutation is required for code acceptance; attended provider proof is a later promotion gate.

## Claim boundary

This is recovery plumbing, not managed continuity proof. TIN-2057 remains unchanged until a separately authorized attended handoff/repair gate passes.

before.title: Exact-model Claude route readiness across N accounts: evidence, staleness, and leases
before.description:
## v0.2 role

Provide exact-model route readiness for the managed Claude broker across N enrolled accounts. Credentials remain account-scoped; there is no per-model credential refresh. Model demand comes from the request body's exact `model` value and must not be silently downgraded.

## Evidence and confidence

* Live traffic headers are highest-confidence observations. The committed Anthropic unified 5-hour/7-day header fixture is account-level unless evidence proves a narrower scope.
* `GET /api/oauth/usage` is an undocumented default advisory input only. Parse tolerantly with required-field checks, cache briefly, attach provenance/freshness, and disable only this source on schema drift.
* Known exhausted-with-reset remains trusted until reset. Known available expires on a freshness deadline. Unknown is eligible for reactive proof but ranks below known-good and above dead/quarantined.
* Missing observations never manufacture model parity or capacity; the broker falls back to reactive request-boundary classification.

## Routing contract

Fold observations into the existing `provider:account#capability` health key and pure quota bucket core. Exact-model eligible routes are selected with sticky least-loaded session leases and identity-family collapse. Shared cross-process lease state must be bounded, redacted, stale-PID recoverable, and advisory rather than a credential authority.

## Acceptance

1. The Claude proxy extracts and preserves the exact model on every attempt.
2. Two accounts can carry different evidence/freshness for the same model without conflating credential health.
3. Unknown/known-good/exhausted/dead ordering and asymmetric staleness are property-tested with injected time.
4. Advisory usage schema drift degrades to reactive routing without ending the session.
5. Concurrent sidecars share lease pressure without starvation at 20 sessions/50 accounts.
6. Committed evidence clearly distinguishes provider-observed model data from account-level inference.

before.title: Claude proxy product gate: strict performance, bounded replay memory, and concurrency
before.description:
## Outcome

Gate the managed Claude proxy on measured product performance and exact-once correctness, not micro-optimization claims.

## Required budgets

* Local routing/auth overhead before upstream I/O: p95 <= 5 ms, p99 <= 10 ms.
* Sustained SSE throughput: within 5% of direct Claude Code.
* Idle sidecar RSS: <= 20 MiB.
* No starvation at 20 concurrent managed sessions across 50 enrolled accounts.
* Replay memory: 32 MiB/request, 64 MiB/sidecar, 256 MiB/host. Use atomic cross-process reservations with stale-PID cleanup.
* Missing reservation or chunked/unknown-length overflow degrades to stream-once with backpressure; never disk spool.

## Correctness

At most two upstream attempts. Only explicit pre-body 401/403/429 can select one alternate. Provider 5xx passes through. Ambiguous transport, cancellation, partial writes, and started responses never cross accounts. Health/state writes must be atomic and state-change-bounded.

Persistent HTTP clients, buffered header parsing, and parse/write deduplication are implementation tools only when measurement justifies them; do not buffer successful SSE bodies.

## Acceptance

A deterministic fake Anthropic upstream plus a direct-vs-proxy benchmark publishes redacted artifacts for latency percentiles, throughput, RSS, memory-pressure fallback, stale reservation cleanup, attempt counts, and 20x50 lock fairness. This blocks TIN-2057.

* Replay memory: 32 MiB/request, 64 MiB/sidecar, 256 MiB/host. Use atomic cross-process reservations with stale-PID cleanup.

## Correctness

At most two upstream attempts. Only explicit pre-body 401/403/429 can select one alternate. Provider 5xx passes through. Ambiguous transport, cancellation, partial writes, and started responses never cross accounts. Health/state writes must be atomic and state-change-bounded.

Persistent HTTP clients, buffered header parsing, and parse/write deduplication are implementation tools only when measurement justifies them; do not buffer successful SSE bodies.

## Acceptance

A deterministic fake Anthropic upstream plus a direct-vs-proxy benchmark publishes redacted artifacts for latency percentiles, throughput, RSS, memory-pressure fallback, stale reservation cleanup, attempt counts, and 20x50 lock fairness. This blocks TIN-2057.
