before.title: Bounded request-boundary lock wait and one-alternate re-election
before.description:
## Problem

Request-boundary refresh/materialization can block indefinitely on a sibling session's per-account flock and make the managed harness appear hung.

## Contract

* Use the existing announced per-account flock shared with resident keepalive.
* Bound lock acquisition by the remaining request deadline; never wait indefinitely.
* A locked candidate is unavailable for that election round and may cause re-election only within the request's single cross-account alternate budget.
* Never select a third account or retry an ambiguous/started request.
* Emit a typed redacted lock-wait/skip event.
* If no route is selectable, apply the program's all-exhausted rule: one wait only for a trusted reset within 30 seconds and the request deadline, then typed 429 plus Retry-After.

## Acceptance

Synthetic concurrent-process tests hold the first and alternate locks, prove bounded completion, attempts <=2, no deadlock with resident refresh, and either success on the sole eligible alternate or a classified terminal result.

`omux claude` launches one managed Claude Code authority process -> C1 serves the context with the exact requested model -> C1 returns a provider-originated, explicitly classified pre-body `quota_exhausted` 429 -> the same sidecar elects one distinct provider identity C2 and replays once -> the same Claude process and native context complete with the byte-identical model and no login or restart.

* one locally derived process fingerprint unchanged before, during, and after the arrow, persisted only as a run-local opaque handle;

* one opaque request handle, exactly two upstream attempts, one alternate, no same-route retry, no third attempt, and no wait beyond the request deadline or 30 seconds;

* no cross-identity replay after body bytes, ambiguity, partial send, cancellation, 5xx, or replay-budget overflow;

Do not persist raw PIDs, stable identity hashes, account labels, emails, filesystem paths, prompts, responses, bodies, environments, or credentials. before.title: Versioned process/JSON-RPC harness adapter contract + OpenCode conformance
before.description:
## Outcome

Freeze the v0.2 process-level harness adapter contract and prove it with Codex, Claude, and OpenCode. Control and redacted diagnostics use a versioned JSON-RPC subprocess boundary. There is no C ABI or shared-library SDK.

## Contract

* opaque session and route handles; no token bytes cross the adapter boundary;
* lifecycle: preflight, managed launch, route/lease snapshot, typed transition, repair handoff, teardown;
* exact-model demand and one-alternate outcome vocabulary shared across adapters;
* feature/status discovery is explicit per method; unimplemented methods cannot advertise support;
* local-only redacted events and stable schema versioning;
* adapter-specific auth/provider mechanics stay behind the process boundary.

## Acceptance

1. Checked-in schema and compatibility tests for the new surface version.
2. Codex and Claude managed adapters round-trip lifecycle and redacted status.
3. OpenCode exercises the same contract as the independent conformance adapter.
4. Only the versioned typed scalar extension namespace is tolerated; all other unknown or sensitive fields fail closed, and unsupported capabilities fail explicitly.
5. No C header, shared library, FFI ownership model, or raw credential response is shipped.

Phase-1 PR #475 declares the surface as `planned_unshipped` / `not_implemented`; it does not satisfy adapter round-trip or OpenCode acceptance.

## Acceptance and evidence gate

Experimental, unshipped native reset. Install Omux, authorize sources once, and use ordinary application commands. Supported handoff preserves the same process and native session/history/tools/approvals with no routine prompt. No wrapper, alternate home, restart, shipped Codex fork, browser automation or synthetic promotion proves this outcome.

Authority: [active reset](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/plans/omux-native-account-lifecycle-reset-2026-10-02.md>), [charter](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/product/charter.md>), [acceptance](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/product/user-stories.md>), [support gates](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/product/support-and-completeness.md>), [evidence](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/implementation/native-reset-evidence-2026-10-02.md>). ## Historical ticket scope — superseded where conflicting

Preserved below for release/intent provenance. July wrapper/GF/optional-daemon/build.zig.zon execution instructions are not actionable current authority.

## Outcome

Freeze the v0.2 process-level harness adapter contract and prove it with Codex, Claude, and OpenCode. Control and redacted diagnostics use a versioned JSON-RPC subprocess boundary. There is no C ABI or shared-library SDK.

## Contract

* opaque session and route handles; no token bytes cross the adapter boundary;
* lifecycle: preflight, managed launch, route/lease snapshot, typed transition, repair handoff, teardown;
* exact-model demand and one-alternate outcome vocabulary shared across adapters;
* feature/status discovery is explicit per method; unimplemented methods cannot advertise support;
* local-only redacted events and stable schema versioning;
* adapter-specific auth/provider mechanics stay behind the process boundary.

## Acceptance

1. Checked-in schema and compatibility tests for the new surface version.
2. Codex and Claude managed adapters round-trip lifecycle and redacted status.
3. OpenCode exercises the same contract as the independent conformance adapter.
4. Only the versioned typed scalar extension namespace is tolerated; all other unknown or sensitive fields fail closed, and unsupported capabilities fail explicitly.
5. No C header, shared library, FFI ownership model, or raw credential response is shipped.

Phase-1 PR #475 declares the surface as `planned_unshipped` / `not_implemented`; it does not satisfy adapter round-trip or OpenCode acceptance.

before.title: Narrow provider seam for Claude, Codex, and OpenCode managed adapters
before.description:
## v0.2 role

Remove Codex-only branching only where the ratified Claude/Codex/OpenCode managed adapter contract needs a shared seam. This is not a universal-provider abstraction.

## Scope

* Preserve byte-compatible Codex behavior.
* Let Claude resolve its declared credential-store and identity rules without hardcoded provider switches in generic control paths.
* Let OpenCode exercise surface_version:2 as a conformance adapter without inheriting Claude/Codex OAuth.
* Keep provider-specific HTTP, enrollment, and credential grammar in adapter modules.
* Do not add Gemini subscription OAuth or revive removed public provider built-ins.

## Acceptance

* The three managed adapters share only proven lifecycle/control types.
* Adding a non-product provider still requires an explicit product/evidence decision.
* Remote tests prove Codex unchanged and Claude fixed-origin sidecar wiring remains provider-specific.

before.title: ProviderDefinition: declare OS-mediated credential stores (keychain derivation, identity claims, reauth browser isolation)
before.description:
From the designated auth-state-model taxonomy (`docs/spec/auth-state-models-and-adapter-extensibility-2026-06-12.md`): the `ProviderDefinition` contract encodes only the home-scoped-file model (codex). The os-keystore-singleton model (claude on macOS) is currently hardcoded across `claudeKeychainService`, `applyClaudeKeychainDefaults`, and decision docs. Make it declarable so the extensibility claim ("one declarative contract expressing BOTH anchor models") becomes true.

**In scope (schema + plumbing, per the spec's Objectives section):**

1. `os_credential_store: ?OsCredentialStore` on ProviderDefinition — first variant `keychain: { base_service, suffix: config_dir_sha256_8, account: local_user }`; `applyClaudeKeychainDefaults` reads the declaration instead of hardcoding claude.
2. `identity: { file, claims }` (e.g. `.claude.json` + `oauthAccount.accountUuid`) so identity-keyed health/stats/dedupe (#359/#360 lane) stops special-casing providers.
3. `reauth.browser_isolation: { incognito_first, ephemeral_profile }` — the TIN-2071 requirement as schema, enforced by the mediated-login flow.
4. Injection-mode truth: gate `credential_template` use on absence of an active `os_credential_store` for the (provider, platform); per-platform hybrid expressible (claude Linux file lane vs macOS keychain).

**Out of scope**: Linux/Windows keystore write ports (separate proofs); collapsing the adapter layer; the #354 contract amendment itself (this informs it).

**Acceptance**: claude's macOS keychain behavior is fully driven by its declared `os_credential_store` (the hardcoded derivation path deleted or reduced to the generic engine); a fixture-only definition for a hypothetical second keychain harness round-trips read/write derivation in tests; docs claim-scope (adoption/onboarding) can drop the "needs compiled support" carve-out for declared keystore providers.

Make it declarable so the extensibility claim ("one declarative contract expressing BOTH anchor models") becomes true.

**In scope (schema + plumbing, per the spec's Objectives section):**

1. `os_credential_store: ?OsCredentialStore` on ProviderDefinition — first variant `keychain: { base_service, suffix: config_dir_sha256_8, account: local_user }`; `applyClaudeKeychainDefaults` reads the declaration instead of hardcoding claude.
2. `identity: { file, claims }` (e.g. `.claude.json` + `oauthAccount.accountUuid`) so identity-keyed health/stats/dedupe (#359/#360 lane) stops special-casing providers.
3. `reauth.browser_isolation: { incognito_first, ephemeral_profile }` — the TIN-2071 requirement as schema, enforced by the mediated-login flow.
4. Injection-mode truth: gate `credential_template` use on absence of an active `os_credential_store` for the (provider, platform); per-platform hybrid expressible (claude Linux file lane vs macOS keychain).

**Out of scope**: Linux/Windows keystore write ports (separate proofs); collapsing the adapter layer; the #354 contract amendment itself (this informs it).

before.title: v0.2 beta adoption proof: three clean non-maintainer installs including Linux
before.description:
## Outcome

Before calling v0.2 market-ready beta, three non-maintainer users complete the public install-to-repair story using only published artifacts and public documentation. At least one user runs a supported Linux systemd/secret-tool environment.

## Acceptance

* Each user starts from a clean machine/user profile with no maintainer config, private Tinyland/GF access, or hand-authored oauth-mux JSON.
* A signed prerelease installs through a supported public lane and exposes `omux` primary plus the documented `oauth-mux` compatibility link.
* `omux setup` guides provider-owned enrollment, identity/model verification, explicit refresh/switch consent, service enablement, and readiness proof.
* The user starts a managed Claude or Codex session, observes a redacted route transition, and completes the documented repair/rollback path.
* One user proves Linux systemd-user plus secret-tool; macOS users prove LaunchAgent behavior.
* Support requests, elapsed setup time, failed steps, and required maintainer interventions are recorded. Any undisclosed maintainer intervention fails the clean-user run.
* Evidence contains no tokens, cookies, raw emails/account ids, prompts, request bodies, or private infrastructure data.
* All three runs cite the exact signed release, checksums/provenance, public docs commit, OS, install lane, and redacted result.

## Claim boundary

Maintainer dogfood, synthetic CI, source-checkout installs, and the existing five-account lab cohort do not count toward this gate. This ticket begins only after the signed prerelease and golden managed-handoff candidate exist.

before.title: GOLDEN METRIC v0.2: one-click managed Claude + Codex continuity with model parity
before.description:
## Product bar

An engineer installs the exact signed v0.2 candidate, enrolls operator-owned or organization-authorized accounts, and runs `omux <harness>`. When the active route exhausts eligible capacity, the same harness process preserves its context and exact requested model, uses one safe alternate, and completes without login, repair, relaunch, resume, or restart.

Repo authority: `docs/runbooks/omux-v0.2-evaluation-ladder-2026-07-14.md` and the v0.2 program linked from GitHub #463.

## Current score

**0/11 on current main** `c9dce4676481e9e7c64e96b2391f8f7332d8d419`**.** PR #521 merged signed candidate `b7f75c3ef1983ac07a468106c83c366abd0af722`; its merge tree exactly matches candidate tree `fb687a17328c7ac84e13bdb2c252f4b4e57096ed`. PR CI `31615091113` passed 9/9, Public Source `31615091160`, GF Test `31615102924`, and GF Check `31615114787` passed. Immutable Stage 2 run `31615220797` intentionally failed the incomplete 124-predicate gate while its downloaded artifact independently reconciled byte-for-byte to **82** **pass / 0 fail /** **42** **missing** from 113 value-free observations. Post-merge CI `31617244004` passed 9/9 and Public Source `31617243991` passed. G4 remains **0/6**. A golden row moves only from committed, redacted evidence for one exact candidate accepted on this issue.

## Golden rows

 1. **G1 Claude continuity:** one Claude process and context survive a provider-originated pre-body `quota_exhausted` 429 through exactly one distinct-identity `C1 -> C2` alternate with the exact model.
 2. **G2 replay memory safety:** ambiguity, partial send, cancellation, started response, 5xx, oversize, and exhausted budgets never cross identities or persist request bytes.
 3. **G3 exact-model readiness and leases:** exact-model evidence, asymmetric staleness, advisory kill-switch/reactive fallback, sticky least-loaded selection, and deterministic shared leases pass.
 4. **G4 performance:** the dedicated GF benchmark passes every pinned latency, throughput, memory, concurrency, and starvation predicate.
 5. **G5 managed boundary and redaction:** carrier, loopback, fixed origin, auth stripping, redirect/SSRF refusal, zero-call rejection, teardown, and allowlist-only evidence pass.
 6. **G6 resident independence:** resident absence or an allowed restart cannot make it the session proxy, expose request bodies, or corrupt the managed session.
 7. **G7 distribution and rollback:** signed macOS and Linux-beta install/upgrade, explicit unsupported Windows behavior, exact installed provenance, and rollback pass.
 8. **G8 Codex continuity:** one Codex process and context survive provider-originated exhaustion through exactly one distinct-identity `X1 -> X2` alternate with the exact model.
 9. **G9 OpenCode conformance:** OpenCode proves the surface-v2 lifecycle, route/lease vocabulary, bounded failure, redaction, compatibility, and explicit unsupported behavior.
10. **G10 bounded failure:** all-exhausted and resident-unavailable cases end once with a typed outcome and trusted `Retry-After`, without loops, invented capacity, or restart.
11. **G11 beta cohort:** three clean non-maintainer users, including one Linux user, complete install, enrollment, managed launch, handoff, repair, and rollback on the exact candidate.

## Trigger and claim boundary

The live G1/G8 trigger is provider-originated quota exhaustion. Pre-body 401/403 remain required synthetic negative coverage but do not substitute for the live continuity trigger. Stages 0-3 are prerequisites and earn no row. Stage 4 installed/service dogfood remains blocked until TIN-1759 is Done with accepted proof and the ladder's O-OWNERSHIP and R-TIN-1759 gates are accepted. v0.1.15 stays the stable shipped release until promotion is explicitly accepted.

Expose one no-spend, token-free view of managed route readiness for operators, agents, and the later read-only menu-bar snapshot.

* Golden JSON tests cover all stable states and redaction.
* status/statusline/doctor agree on the same reducer output.
* Unknown ranks below known-good and above dead/quarantined.
* Remote check passes.

A cassette fixture proves redaction and schema shape without raw cookies, tokens, emails, account IDs, PII screenshots, prompts, or response bodies. Browser-observed data is labeled observational and cannot establish a provider API contract or singleton-switch continuity.

No production scraping dependency, canonical-keychain mutation, hidden spend, provider bypass, or acceptance gate for TIN-2057.

before.title: Consume the Zig-emitted release manifest across supported install lanes
before.description:
## Authority

`build.zig.zon` is the single human-edited version source and the Zig release graph owns target/product semantics. It deterministically emits and checks `release-manifest.json`. Consumers do not own independent versions or target lists.

## In scope

* GitHub release assets and checksums/signing inputs.
* Curl installer.
* Binary-only Homebrew formula.
* deb/rpm metadata.
* Nix/source consumption.
* Compatibility `oauth-mux` link beside primary `omux`.
* Service assets, SBOM/provenance, build ID, adapter protocol versions, and supported-platform declarations.

## Excluded

npm remains retired. Do not add `.pkg`, `.dmg`, AppImage, or another unratified lane. Windows managed broker is unsupported; any retained v0.1.15 artifact is compatibility history until the manifest explicitly removes it.

## Acceptance

One `build.zig.zon` version change causes the Zig graph to regenerate/check every supported consumer with no hand-edited drift. Clean-source and installed-artifact proofs agree on version, hashes, signatures, SBOM, provenance, and support matrix.

before.title: Week 1 CLI contract: install `omux` primary with `oauth-mux` compatibility link
before.description:
## Outcome

Define and implement the v0.2 executable naming boundary before feature code depends on it: public docs and new managed commands use `omux`; existing v0.1 users retain `oauth-mux` as a compatibility link to the same signed binary during the migration window.

## Scope

* Make one binary serve both names without divergent behavior, version, config, or telemetry.
* `omux setup`, `omux claude`, `omux codex`, `omux status`, `omux doctor`, `omux service`, `omux repair`, and `omux version` are the eventual public v0.2 command set.
* Week 1 may land the naming/install contract and characterization tests before every command exists.
* Packaging and the Zig-emitted release manifest declare both executable names from one product artifact.
* Existing scripts and stable docs are migrated deliberately; no shell alias or second independently-versioned package.
* Windows managed broker remains unsupported even if the stable v0.1.15 binary artifact persists.

## Acceptance

* Invoking either name reports the same version/build id and reads the same config/state roots.
* Homebrew, curl, Nix, deb/rpm, and source installs consume the generated compatibility mapping when the manifest lane lands.
* Upgrade/uninstall tests leave no dangling duplicate binary.
* Public prerelease docs use `omux` as primary and state the compatibility window.
* GloriousFlywheel remote check and release proof pass.

before.title: Keepalive service residency addendum: doctor version/SHA surfacing, stale-binary warn, PATH-shadow detect, systemd leg
before.description:
## What

Split from TIN-1830 per operator decision 2026-07-09 (see closing comment there). Service residency itself is PROVEN (#444, `docs/evidence/keepalive-service-residency-20260704T161515Z/`, shipped v0.1.14); this ticket is the operability tail.

## Acceptance

* `doctor` reports the resident service binary's version + SHA and the PATH-resolved binary's version + SHA, side by side.
* Warn when the resident binary is older than the installed binary (offline-safe compare; sibling of TIN-2463's `version --check`).
* PATH-shadow detection: multiple `oauth-mux` on PATH → report all, state which wins (the 2026-07-04→07 shadow on neo was live-observed; currently benign, mechanism persists).
* systemd-user leg proven on a Linux host with a dated `docs/evidence/` dir.
* Remote lanes green before any completion claim.

## Priority note

High because managed broker work is active. The relevant lineage is the authenticated per-session Claude sidecar (TIN-1829) and same-process handoff proof (TIN-2077), not canceled TIN-2721 canonical-keychain mutation. A stale resident can still provide incorrect refresh/observation state to managed sessions even though it does not own the sidecar request path.

## Current host gate (2026-07-13)

The macOS upgrade/restart dogfood is paused on TIN-1759. The shared GUI launchd domain still exposes direct secret-bearing variables; narrow and activate that host policy before restarting the service, then capture minimal-environment and `stale=false` evidence. This is a host custody dependency, not an oauth-mux binary defect.

before.title: v0.2 FOSS readiness: contribution, security, privacy, support, and fork-proof policy
before.description:
## Why

Market-ready FOSS requires a stranger to understand how to build, report vulnerabilities, contribute, verify releases, and know what data stays local. Today those promises are scattered across old roadmaps and package docs.

## Scope

* Add or truth current `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, support matrix, privacy/local-data statement, migration guide, issue/PR templates, and release verification instructions.
* Public command/support matrix: macOS GA target, Linux beta, Windows managed broker unsupported; v0.1.15 stable until the v0.2 golden gate.
* Document fork policy: untrusted fork PRs execute no credentialed/private CI; contributors run public local checks; a maintainer promotes a trusted commit/branch for GloriousFlywheel remote proof.
* Ensure source builds and prerelease verification need no private endpoints or secrets.
* Publish dependency/license, SBOM/provenance, signing, checksum, and vulnerability-reporting boundaries.
* Keep browser/cookie-picker evidence explicitly operator-assisted and exclude cookies, tokens, raw account ids/emails, and PII screenshots.

## Acceptance

1. A clean non-maintainer can build, test, install a signed prerelease, verify checksums/provenance, and file a safe report using only public docs.
2. Fork PR behavior is tested and cannot execute privileged GF/provider lanes.
3. Security policy names the local loopback sidecar threat boundary and private reporting path without promising unsupported response SLAs.
4. Privacy copy matches local-only telemetry and no prompt/body persistence.
5. Docs are linked from README and the release/migration runbooks and pass remote proof.

## Outcome

Make per-account browser isolation a guided `omux setup` enrollment property, not a background reauth engine or runtime broker dependency.

Live evidence from TIN-2060 showed that a second Claude account can inherit the first account's browser session and fail to reach fresh consent/code delivery. Each provider-owned login therefore opens in a fresh private or ephemeral browser context.

* Runtime continuity uses the TIN-1829 sidecar and never depends on a browser.
* No custom reauth-job or flow-composition product is revived.

* Two consecutive account enrollments each reach a fresh provider-owned login/consent surface.
* The resulting accounts have distinct isolated config/keychain identities.
* Tests and redacted evidence contain no cookies, token bytes, raw emails, or screenshots with PII.
* The flow returns to `omux setup`, verifies identity/model signals, and records explicit consent before admission.

before.title: omux setup: guided account enrollment, consent, service enablement, and readiness proof
before.description:
## Outcome

A clean user reaches a ready managed Claude/Codex fleet through one guided `omux setup` flow without insider topology knowledge or hand-edited JSON.

## Flow

1. Preflight platform, harness binaries, keychain/secret-tool, service support, PATH/version truth, and existing config.
2. Collect labeled operator-owned accounts and desired Claude/Codex harnesses.
3. Stage isolated per-account stores and launch provider-owned login, one isolated browser context per identity.
4. Verify redacted identity uniqueness, declared model demand, entitlement/signal provenance, and account health.
5. Ask separately for consent to proactive refresh and managed switching; default deny on ambiguity.
6. Install/enable the user refresh/observation service only after confirmation.
7. Run a bounded readiness proof and print precise `omux repair <label>` actions for failures.

## Boundaries

No cookie import as auth, no hidden browser automation, no credential pooling, no daemon-required request proxy, and no broad provider wizard. Agent-safe JSON plan mode must not prompt or read secrets.

## Acceptance

Three steps or fewer from clean install to staged logins/readiness; idempotent rerun; no hand-edited config; macOS live proof and Linux systemd/secret-tool beta proof; redacted clean-user evidence.

before.title: Release discipline: evidence-bound cut cadence, CHANGELOG maintenance, CI tag-drift warning
before.description:
## Problem

61 PRs sat unreleased between v0.1.13 (2026-06-12) and v0.1.14 (2026-07-04) with zero signal — every packaged install lane served a binary predating the `oauth-mux keepalive` command, and the operator's own stale binary panicked mid-dogfood. There was no cadence, no CHANGELOG, and nothing that warns when the release channel drifts from main.

## Shipped already (PR #441, the v0.1.14 cut)

`CHANGELOG.md` exists with the discipline stated in its header: **cuts are bound to committed** `docs/evidence/` **dirs; claims stop at that evidence; a cut is owed whenever a flagship evidence dir lands.**

## Remaining scope

1. **CI tag-drift warning**: a cheap job (or PR-comment bot step) that computes `commits-ahead` and `days-ahead` of main vs the latest `v*` tag and warns on PRs when either crosses a threshold (propose: 20 commits or 14 days). Warning, never a gate.
2. **Runbook update**: fold the cadence rule + CHANGELOG maintenance into `docs/release-runbook.md` (currently updated 2026-05-09, pre-dates all of this).
3. **CHANGELOG gate**: the release-proof lane checks the tag's version has a CHANGELOG entry (fail the cut, not PRs).

Cross-refs: TIN-2050 (SSOT-derived lane generation — owns the lanes themselves, not the cadence), TIN-1830 (running-binary version/SHA visibility acceptance), TIN-2409 (Done — the stale-binary panic history). Posture: distribution-not-hosted; nothing here phones home.

— filed by deliverable-shape review (verified SOUND_WITH_FIXES), operator-approved 2026-07-04, session 9925b2e2; dup-checked (no existing cadence/CHANGELOG ticket for omux).

before.description:
## Why

The repo now has a real public release, but adoption needs a website that explains the problem, shows the typed fallback model, and gives users one copyable path to try the tool safely.

## Scope

* Build a devtool-focused website, not a generic marketing splash.
* First viewport: `oauth-mux`, typed OAuth fallback, install command, and real redacted CLI/JSON output.
* Include sections for problem, fallback algebra, install surfaces, first-run Codex flow, agent discovery, privacy/security, provider status matrix, and provider contribution.
* Clearly separate `live-proven`, `schema-modeled`, and `planned` provider support.
* Link README, npm, GitHub release, provider checklist, live QA docs, daemon boundary, and rollback docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Public page is live and linked from README or release notes.
* Copy uses precise support claims: Codex live-proven, other providers not overclaimed.
* Site has a feedback/contribution path for provider authors.
* Launch snippets are ready for soft-launch posts.

before.title: Health-key codec: reject separator collisions and overflow at config validation
before.description:
## Problem

TIN-3006 review found a broader pre-existing invariant gap outside its three-file charter.

`src/health.zig` encodes route state into a fixed 256-byte `provider:account#capability` key. `KeyBuf.append` silently truncates, and `parseHealthKey` interprets the first `#` after the provider/account separator as the capability boundary. Current config validation rejects `:` in provider names but does not reject `#` in account/capability names or prove that every configured account/capability key fits losslessly.

That permits two configured routes to collide or become unparseable in persisted health state. TIN-3006 fails closed at its new planning front doors, but it must not expand into shared config/health ownership.

## Scope

* Define one lossless health-key constructor/validator shared by config and runtime users.
* Reject reserved separators in account and capability names at config validation.
* Reject any configured account or capability route whose encoded key exceeds the codec limit; do not truncate.
* Cover custom provider definitions as well as built-ins.
* Preserve valid colon-containing account labels if the codec/parser contract intentionally supports them.
* Audit all direct `accountKey`/`capabilityKey` callers for silent-truncation assumptions.

## Acceptance

* Config validation fails with field-specific errors for `#` collisions and overlong account/capability routes.
* Property/boundary tests prove encode/parse round-trip and uniqueness for all accepted keys.
* No runtime health path can create a truncated key.
* Existing valid config and emitted compatibility bytes remain unchanged.
* Exact-head GF Test and GF Check pass.

## Claim boundary

This is route-state integrity hardening. It does not move Stage 4, G11, or TIN-2057 and does not authorize credential/provider access.

before.title: Claude managed adapter: authenticated per-session ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL request proxy
before.description:
## Outcome

Implement the v0.2 managed Claude adapter as a per-session authenticated loopback request proxy. `omux claude [-- <args>]` launches Claude Code with an ephemeral `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and a base64url 256-bit capability in `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`. Bare `claude` is untouched.

## Contract

* Bind loopback only; keep the capability memory-only, compare in constant time, strip it upstream, and return local 401 with zero upstream calls on mismatch. An instrumented launch must prove Claude Code's bearer carrier before claiming this boundary.
* Forward origin-form requests only to compile-fixed `https://api.anthropic.com`; reject CONNECT, absolute-form, arbitrary destinations, caller-selected upstreams, and credential-carrying redirects.
* Strip inbound auth/API-key headers and inject only the elected account's OAuth credential.
* Preserve the exact requested model.
* Permit one cross-account alternate only for explicit pre-body 401/403/429. Provider 5xx passes through. Never replay started responses or ambiguous transport outcomes.
* Replay budgets are 32 MiB/request, 64 MiB/sidecar, and 256 MiB/host with atomic reservations/stale-PID cleanup. Budget or chunked overflow becomes stream-once; no disk spooling.
* Refresh at request boundary through the existing per-account flock. Hard rotating-refresh-token failure quarantines the route and requires provider-owned re-enrollment; never restore stale token backups.
* When all routes are exhausted, wait once only for a trusted reset within 30 seconds and the request deadline, then typed 429 plus Retry-After.
* The resident service remains refresh/observation/alert/snapshot only, never the request proxy.

## First proof

A deterministic fake Anthropic upstream proves carrier behavior, bad-token zero-call rejection, fixed-origin/redirect negatives, streaming pass-through, exact-model preservation, single-alternate 401/403/429, 5xx pass-through, ambiguous/started exclusions, replay budgets, cleanup, and redaction. Live proof follows under TIN-2077.

before.title: Flip shouldPreserveChildAuth to broker-owned-only (single-writer invariant)
before.description:
**Epic:** zig-core · **Size:** M · **Depends on:** CredentialLock

WHAT: `shouldPreserveChildAuth` (`src/adapters/codex/wire_proxy.zig:1645-1654`, called at `:1622`) returns true whenever the child's inbound `ChatGPT-Account-ID` equals the elected account (test `:2484-2489`), letting the CHILD rotate the shared token — the second half of the incident. Gate on an explicit `broker_is_sole_writer` flag threaded from session config rather than account-id equality; the proxy always injects the broker's elected token and never preserves child-supplied auth for a managed account.

WHY: even a flock-guarded broker can be undercut by the child as a second uncoordinated writer.

ACCEPTANCE: unit test asserts it never preserves for a managed account; `scripts/smoke-codex-child-refresh.sh` green; concurrent-sessions smoke shows no `token_revoked`.

before.title: claudeKeychainService default-dir contradiction: derivation always suffixes but ~/.claude should use the base service (TIN-2060 edge)
before.description:
Surfaced by the TIN-2054-#2 review (confirmed latent, pre-existing — not introduced by the guard).

`provider_schema.claudeKeychainService` ALWAYS appends a `-<sha256(dir)[:8]>` suffix, yet its own doc-comment (and the TIN-2060 proof) states the default dir `~/.claude` uses the **unsuffixed base** `Claude Code-credentials` (the service bare Claude Code uses when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is unset). So:

* A managed Claude account configured with `config_dir: "~/.claude"` (or `$HOME/.claude`) and `service: null` derives `Claude Code-credentials-<hash(~/.claude)>` — the **wrong** service. The real item for that dir is (per the bare-CLI contract) the unsuffixed base, so oauth-mux would **read/write a non-existent/foreign keychain item** → the account is broken at the read layer before refresh ever runs.
* The TIN-2054-#2 canonical-keychain guard (exact-match on the unsuffixed base) therefore CANNOT catch this suffixed-but-wrong form. It only protects the literal base-string form (what `omux init` produces, and what the live `personal` account uses). The `~/.claude`-as-config_dir case is independently malfunctioning, so practical revoke-risk is low — but the comment-vs-code contradiction is a real latent defect.

**Root unknown (TIN-2060):** does the Claude CLI use the suffixed or the base service when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is exported AND equals the default `~/.claude`? Resolve it, then:

* **(a)** special-case `claudeKeychainService` to return the unsuffixed base when the absolute dir equals the resolved `~/.claude` (so the derived service matches the CLI's, and the canonical guard's exact-match correctly catches the only true bare-Claude form); OR

Surfaced by the TIN-2054-#2 review (confirmed latent, pre-existing — not introduced by the guard).

`provider_schema.claudeKeychainService` ALWAYS appends a `-<sha256(dir)[:8]>` suffix, yet its own doc-comment (and the TIN-2060 proof) states the default dir `~/.claude` uses the **unsuffixed base** `Claude Code-credentials` (the service bare Claude Code uses when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is unset). Unbounded state growth: every managed run writes `state/codex/status/managed-<ts>.ndjson` (483 files observed; up to 525KB each); smoke commands leave `codex-broker-*-smoke-<ts>` dirs; `latestCodexStatusPath` stat-sweeps the whole dir per `codex status` (`src/main.zig:11087-11113`). Per-account homes also accumulate `sessions/` rollouts with no sweep (acknowledged TIN-1851 follow-up).

**In scope**: keep-last-N (configurable) prune of status files + smoke dirs at session start; bounded, opt-in `sessions/` retention sweep per account home (default: keep everything until explicitly enabled — sessions are user data).

**Out of scope**: canonical ~/.codex (never ours to prune).

**Acceptance**: status dir bounded after N runs; sessions sweep refuses to run without explicit config/flag; sweep never touches a home whose account lock is held.

A reviewable completion attaches exact revision/artifact/platform/native/provider tuple, declared action receipt, predicates and limitations. Native/live/real-vault/installed gates remain unrun or blocked until their actual receipts exist. Dependencies are reconciled by links, not synthetic score.

## Historical ticket scope — superseded where conflicting

Preserved below for release/intent provenance. July wrapper/GF/optional-daemon/build.zig.zon execution instructions are not actionable current authority.

## Outcome

A route in `hard_lineage_invalidated` can return to service only through one managed, provider-owned re-enrollment transaction that proves a newly issued credential lineage and durably resolves both hard authorities. Raw provider login by itself is not clearance.

## Contract

* Acquire the existing per-provider/account flock and the exact upstream-identity flock when available.
* Snapshot only redacted pre-enrollment generation/fingerprint evidence in memory; never persist tokens or provider response bodies.
* Launch the provider-owned login in the account's isolated config/browser boundary.
* Re-read the canonical credential under the same transaction and prove a fresh usable access token plus refresh token and a new credential generation. Same identity is allowed; stale or unchanged rotating-token lineage is not.
* Commit a closed `provider_reenroll_resolved` event and marker transition with crash ordering that never exposes a route between marker removal and durable resolution.
* Update the hard-lineage reducer so only that privately constructed resolution proof can clear the prior hard event. Ordinary `refreshed` rows, manual file edits, stale backups, and raw login success remain unable to clear it.
* On any ambiguity or partial persistence, preserve hard quarantine and emit a redacted typed failure.
* Claude/Codex enrollment remains provider-owned; browser isolation follows TIN-2071. Setup/repair presentation follows TIN-3006.

## Acceptance

* Fake-provider tests cover success, unchanged token lineage, identity drift, canceled login, torn credential, lock contention, crash points on both sides of the durable resolution commit, and restart reduction.
* Tests prove stale backup restoration and ordinary refresh/login rows cannot clear hard state.
* Status/doctor expose whether managed clearance is available and the exact safe next action without implying an unavailable flow.
* Exact-head GF test/check, required CI, and Public Source pass.
* No live provider call or installed/service mutation is required for code acceptance; attended provider proof is a later promotion gate.

## Claim boundary

This is recovery plumbing, not managed continuity proof. ## v0.2 role

Provide exact-model route readiness for the managed Claude broker across N enrolled accounts. Credentials remain account-scoped; there is no per-model credential refresh. Model demand comes from the request body's exact `model` value and must not be silently downgraded.

## Evidence and confidence

* Live traffic headers are highest-confidence observations. The committed Anthropic unified 5-hour/7-day header fixture is account-level unless evidence proves a narrower scope.

Fold observations into the existing `provider:account#capability` health key and pure quota bucket core. Exact-model eligible routes are selected with sticky least-loaded session leases and identity-family collapse. Shared cross-process lease state must be bounded, redacted, stale-PID recoverable, and advisory rather than a credential authority.

1. The Claude proxy extracts and preserves the exact model on every attempt.
2. Two accounts can carry different evidence/freshness for the same model without conflating credential health.
3. Unknown/known-good/exhausted/dead ordering and asymmetric staleness are property-tested with injected time.
4. Advisory usage schema drift degrades to reactive routing without ending the session.
5. Concurrent sidecars share lease pressure without starvation at 20 sessions/50 accounts.
6. Committed evidence clearly distinguishes provider-observed model data from account-level inference.

## Acceptance and evidence gate

Experimental, unshipped native reset. Install Omux, authorize sources once, and use ordinary application commands. Supported handoff preserves the same process and native session/history/tools/approvals with no routine prompt. No wrapper, alternate home, restart, shipped Codex fork, browser automation or synthetic promotion proves this outcome.

A reviewable completion attaches exact revision/artifact/platform/native/provider tuple, declared action receipt, predicates and limitations. Native/live/real-vault/installed gates remain unrun or blocked until their actual receipts exist. Dependencies are reconciled by links, not synthetic score.

## Historical ticket scope — superseded where conflicting

Preserved below for release/intent provenance. July wrapper/GF/optional-daemon/build.zig.zon execution instructions are not actionable current authority.

## Outcome

A clean user reaches a ready managed Claude/Codex fleet through one guided `omux setup` flow without insider topology knowledge or hand-edited JSON.

## Flow

1. Preflight platform, harness binaries, keychain/secret-tool, service support, PATH/version truth, and existing config.
2. Collect labeled operator-owned accounts and desired Claude/Codex harnesses.
3. Stage isolated per-account stores and launch provider-owned login, one isolated browser context per identity.
4. Verify redacted identity uniqueness, declared model demand, entitlement/signal provenance, and account health.
5. Ask separately for consent to proactive refresh and managed switching; default deny on ambiguity.
6. Install/enable the user refresh/observation service only after confirmation.
7. Run a bounded readiness proof and print precise `omux repair <label>` actions for failures.

## Boundaries

No cookie import as auth, no hidden browser automation, no credential pooling, no daemon-required request proxy, and no broad provider wizard. Agent-safe JSON plan mode must not prompt or read secrets.

## Acceptance

Three steps or fewer from clean install to staged logins/readiness; idempotent rerun; no hand-edited config; macOS live proof and Linux systemd/secret-tool beta proof; redacted clean-user evidence.","priority":{"value":2,"name":"High"},"url":"https://linear.app/tinyland/issue/TIN-2063/reversible-source-authorization-setup-truthful-repair-jobs","gitBranchName":"jess/tin-2063-reversible-source-authorization-setup-truthful-repair-jobs","createdAt":"2026-06-12T18:51:13.324Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-03T03:58:13.866Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":"2026-07-31T18:04:34.601Z","canceledAt":null,"dueDate":"2026-10-04","slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"In Progress","statusType":"started","labels":[],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Jess Sullivan","createdById":"5402ff97-3cab-4490-9922-b4d20eb0650f","assignee":"Jess Sullivan","assigneeId":"5402ff97-3cab-4490-9922-b4d20eb0650f","project":"Omux · Nix-Bazel delivery + thin clients","projectId":"e3f590ce-5824-4ac6-b13e-4b91ebe22ed2","team":"Tinyland","teamId":"a2c482c8-4d0d-4171-82d9-553265b6c706"}

One `build.zig.zon` version change causes the Zig graph to regenerate/check every supported consumer with no hand-edited drift. ## Existing substrate and historical scope

I-54 and six active projects are reused, not duplicated. Both canceled federation/C ABI projects remain canceled; Done tickets and TIN-491 remain intact. Twenty-four active compatible tickets now carry native scope plus their full predecessor descriptions. Seven incompatible proposals were canceled with replacement links, not deleted. TIN-824 remains website accessibility work.

Historical TIN-2057 0/11 / 82-pass / 42-missing scores remain in its preserved appendix for their exact July candidate. They are not successor proof. v0.1.15 remains historical stable release; new reset remains experimental and unshipped.

From 2026-10-02 23:41:49 EDT / 2026-10-03T03:41:49Z: +3h Oct3 02:41:49 EDT; +5h Oct3 04:41:49 EDT; +10h Oct3 09:41:49 EDT; weekend Oct4 23:59 EDT. REL numeric objectives are adopted measurement targets, unmeasured. Current experimental software has no contractual SLA, service credits, staffed support or human on-call. Severity S0–S3 informs backlog triage only; future agreement response times are proposed terms.

Local source/fixture proof cannot close upstream native availability, ordinary launch/resume/attachment, live compatible handoff, actual Secret Service/Keychain, installed services/desktops, macOS SDK/platform, refresh owner adoption or production browser schemas. Each is an explicit issue dependency/resource gate. Browser acquisition is optional and production exports stay disabled pending proof. Omux ships no Codex fork.

oauth-mux owns runtime/API/capability/release evidence. Official Codex owns native hook acceptance. omux.xoxd.ai owns rendering and exact generated bundle imports, never runtime claims. Gate the managed Claude proxy on measured product performance and exact-once correctness, not micro-optimization claims.

## Required budgets

* Local routing/auth overhead before upstream I/O: p95 <= 5 ms, p99 <= 10 ms.
* Sustained SSE throughput: within 5% of direct Claude Code.
* Idle sidecar RSS: <= 20 MiB.

* Replay memory: 32 MiB/request, 64 MiB/sidecar, 256 MiB/host. Use atomic cross-process reservations with stale-PID cleanup.

Persistent HTTP clients, buffered header parsing, and parse/write deduplication are implementation tools only when measurement justifies them; do not buffer successful SSE bodies.

## Historical initiative — superseded 2026-10-02

## Product bar

Install `omux`, enroll the operator's own accounts once, run `omux claude` or `omux codex`, and preserve the exact requested model across account exhaustion without restarting the harness or prompting for login at a safe request boundary.

## Five product projects

1. **Core + Subtraction** — pure broker types, v0.2 CLI/process contract, main.zig extraction, and deletion of superseded paths.
2. **Claude Managed Broker** — authenticated per-session `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` sidecar, fixed Anthropic origin, exact-model routing, one safe alternate, shared leases, and advisory quota observations.
3. **Adapter Contract + Codex/OpenCode Parity** — Codex remains the reference; OpenCode proves the versioned process/JSON-RPC contract generalizes.
4. **Delivery + FOSS** — `omux setup`, resident refresh/observation service, Zig-emitted release manifest, signed packages, contribution/security/privacy/support surfaces.
5. **Operator Trust + Evidence** — redacted local observability, rollout gates, weekly micro-spend compatibility, golden cohort, and prerelease promotion.

**External non-blocking workstream:** TIN-2105 owns pinned Bazel plus forced Zig/GF REAPI proof. It is related to this initiative, not a sixth product project and not a prerelease blocker.

## Binding decisions

* Managed launch only; bare harnesses remain unmanaged.
* Claude uses a per-session authenticated loopback request proxy to the compile-fixed Anthropic origin.
* Exact model by default; no silent model downgrade.
* One alternate only after explicit pre-body 401/403/429.
* Provider 5xx, ambiguous transport, and started responses never cross accounts.
* Replay caps: 32 MiB/request, 64 MiB/sidecar, 256 MiB/host; no disk spooling.
* An exhausted pool may wait once only for a trusted reset within 30 seconds and the request deadline; otherwise return typed 429 plus Retry-After.
* OAuth usage is advisory and provenance-carrying; reactive fallback remains.
* Local-only product; federation and hosted pooling are canceled.
* `build.zig.zon` and the Zig release graph emit/check the manifest consumed by packages and Bazel/GF.
* Rollout: shadow → manual-route → automatic beta → default managed.
* macOS GA target, Linux beta, Windows managed broker unsupported.
* Signed prereleases; v0.1.15 remains stable until the golden gate.
* Market gate: 2xClaude + 2xCodex, OpenCode conformance, and three clean non-maintainer installs including Linux.
* Performance gate: p95 <=5 ms, p99 <=10 ms, streaming within 5% of direct, idle RSS <=20 MiB, no starvation at 20 sessions/50 accounts.
* Untrusted fork PRs do not execute privileged GF CI; maintainer promotion to a trusted branch precedes authoritative proof.

## Authority

GitHub program: [https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/issues/463](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/issues/463>)

Repo authority packet: `docs/plans/oauth-mux-v0.2-full-broker-foss-program-2026-07-11.md`, `docs/security/omux-v0.2-threat-model-2026-07-11.md`, `docs/authority-map.md`, and the deletion ledger (phase-1 authority PR).

A reviewable completion attaches exact revision/artifact/platform/native/provider tuple, declared action receipt, predicates and limitations. Native/live/real-vault/installed gates remain unrun or blocked until their actual receipts exist. Dependencies are reconciled by links, not synthetic score.

## Historical ticket scope — superseded where conflicting

Preserved below for release/intent provenance. July wrapper/GF/optional-daemon/build.zig.zon execution instructions are not actionable current authority.

## Outcome

A route in `hard_lineage_invalidated` can return to service only through one managed, provider-owned re-enrollment transaction that proves a newly issued credential lineage and durably resolves both hard authorities. Raw provider login by itself is not clearance.

## Contract

* Acquire the existing per-provider/account flock and the exact upstream-identity flock when available.
* Snapshot only redacted pre-enrollment generation/fingerprint evidence in memory; never persist tokens or provider response bodies.
* Launch the provider-owned login in the account's isolated config/browser boundary.
* Re-read the canonical credential under the same transaction and prove a fresh usable access token plus refresh token and a new credential generation. Same identity is allowed; stale or unchanged rotating-token lineage is not.
* Commit a closed `provider_reenroll_resolved` event and marker transition with crash ordering that never exposes a route between marker removal and durable resolution.
* Update the hard-lineage reducer so only that privately constructed resolution proof can clear the prior hard event. Ordinary `refreshed` rows, manual file edits, stale backups, and raw login success remain unable to clear it.
* On any ambiguity or partial persistence, preserve hard quarantine and emit a redacted typed failure.
* Claude/Codex enrollment remains provider-owned; browser isolation follows TIN-2071. Setup/repair presentation follows TIN-3006.

## Acceptance

* Fake-provider tests cover success, unchanged token lineage, identity drift, canceled login, torn credential, lock contention, crash points on both sides of the durable resolution commit, and restart reduction.
* Tests prove stale backup restoration and ordinary refresh/login rows cannot clear hard state.
* Status/doctor expose whether managed clearance is available and the exact safe next action without implying an unavailable flow.
* Exact-head GF test/check, required CI, and Public Source pass.
* No live provider call or installed/service mutation is required for code acceptance; attended provider proof is a later promotion gate.

## Claim boundary

This is recovery plumbing, not managed continuity proof. TIN-2057 remains unchanged until a separately authorized attended handoff/repair gate passes.

A deterministic fake Anthropic upstream plus a direct-vs-proxy benchmark publishes redacted artifacts for latency percentiles, throughput, RSS, memory-pressure fallback, stale reservation cleanup, attempt counts, and 20x50 lock fairness. This blocks TIN-2057.

`omux claude` launches one managed Claude Code authority process -> C1 serves the context with the exact requested model -> C1 returns a provider-originated, explicitly classified pre-body `quota_exhausted` 429 -> the same sidecar elects one distinct provider identity C2 and replays once -> the same Claude process and native context complete with the byte-identical model and no login or restart.

Preserved below for release/intent provenance. July wrapper/GF/optional-daemon/build.zig.zon execution instructions are not actionable current authority.

Remove Codex-only branching only where the ratified Claude/Codex/OpenCode managed adapter contract needs a shared seam. This is not a universal-provider abstraction.

* Preserve byte-compatible Codex behavior.
* Let Claude resolve its declared credential-store and identity rules without hardcoded provider switches in generic control paths.

* The three managed adapters share only proven lifecycle/control types.
* Adding a non-product provider still requires an explicit product/evidence decision.

Program: #463; TIN-1798 owns the versioned process/JSON-RPC contract.

## Historical ticket scope — superseded where conflicting

Preserved below for release/intent provenance. July wrapper/GF/optional-daemon/build.zig.zon execution instructions are not actionable current authority.

From the designated auth-state-model taxonomy (`docs/spec/auth-state-models-and-adapter-extensibility-2026-06-12.md`): the `ProviderDefinition` contract encodes only the home-scoped-file model (codex). The os-keystore-singleton model (claude on macOS) is currently hardcoded across `claudeKeychainService`, `applyClaudeKeychainDefaults`, and decision docs. Make it declarable so the extensibility claim ("one declarative contract expressing BOTH anchor models") becomes true.

**In scope (schema + plumbing, per the spec's Objectives section):**

1. `os_credential_store: ?OsCredentialStore` on ProviderDefinition — first variant `keychain: { base_service, suffix: config_dir_sha256_8, account: local_user }`; `applyClaudeKeychainDefaults` reads the declaration instead of hardcoding claude.
2. `identity: { file, claims }` (e.g. `.claude.json` + `oauthAccount.accountUuid`) so identity-keyed health/stats/dedupe (#359/#360 lane) stops special-casing providers.
3. `reauth.browser_isolation: { incognito_first, ephemeral_profile }` — the TIN-2071 requirement as schema, enforced by the mediated-login flow.
4. Injection-mode truth: gate `credential_template` use on absence of an active `os_credential_store` for the (provider, platform); per-platform hybrid expressible (claude Linux file lane vs macOS keychain).

**Out of scope**: Linux/Windows keystore write ports (separate proofs); collapsing the adapter layer; the #354 contract amendment itself (this informs it).

**Acceptance**: claude's macOS keychain behavior is fully driven by its declared `os_credential_store` (the hardcoded derivation path deleted or reduced to the generic engine); a fixture-only definition for a hypothetical second keychain harness round-trips read/write derivation in tests; docs claim-scope (adoption/onboarding) can drop the "needs compiled support" carve-out for declared keystore providers.

## Product bar

An engineer installs the exact signed v0.2 candidate, enrolls operator-owned or organization-authorized accounts, and runs `omux <harness>`. When the active route exhausts eligible capacity, the same harness process preserves its context and exact requested model, uses one safe alternate, and completes without login, repair, relaunch, resume, or restart.

Repo authority: `docs/runbooks/omux-v0.2-evaluation-ladder-2026-07-14.md` and the v0.2 program linked from GitHub #463.

## Current score

**0/11 on current main** `c9dce4676481e9e7c64e96b2391f8f7332d8d419`**.** PR #521 merged signed candidate `b7f75c3ef1983ac07a468106c83c366abd0af722`; its merge tree exactly matches candidate tree `fb687a17328c7ac84e13bdb2c252f4b4e57096ed`. PR CI `31615091113` passed 9/9, Public Source `31615091160`, GF Test `31615102924`, and GF Check `31615114787` passed. Immutable Stage 2 run `31615220797` intentionally failed the incomplete 124-predicate gate while its downloaded artifact independently reconciled byte-for-byte to **82** **pass / 0 fail /** **42** **missing** from 113 value-free observations. Post-merge CI `31617244004` passed 9/9 and Public Source `31617243991` passed. G4 remains **0/6**. A golden row moves only from committed, redacted evidence for one exact candidate accepted on this issue.

## Golden rows

 1. **G1 Claude continuity:** one Claude process and context survive a provider-originated pre-body `quota_exhausted` 429 through exactly one distinct-identity `C1 -> C2` alternate with the exact model.
 2. **G2 replay memory safety:** ambiguity, partial send, cancellation, started response, 5xx, oversize, and exhausted budgets never cross identities or persist request bytes.
 3. **G3 exact-model readiness and leases:** exact-model evidence, asymmetric staleness, advisory kill-switch/reactive fallback, sticky least-loaded selection, and deterministic shared leases pass.
 4. **G4 performance:** the dedicated GF benchmark passes every pinned latency, throughput, memory, concurrency, and starvation predicate.
 5. **G5 managed boundary and redaction:** carrier, loopback, fixed origin, auth stripping, redirect/SSRF refusal, zero-call rejection, teardown, and allowlist-only evidence pass.
 6. **G6 resident independence:** resident absence or an allowed restart cannot make it the session proxy, expose request bodies, or corrupt the managed session.
 7. **G7 distribution and rollback:** signed macOS and Linux-beta install/upgrade, explicit unsupported Windows behavior, exact installed provenance, and rollback pass.
 8. **G8 Codex continuity:** one Codex process and context survive provider-originated exhaustion through exactly one distinct-identity `X1 -> X2` alternate with the exact model.
 9. **G9 OpenCode conformance:** OpenCode proves the surface-v2 lifecycle, route/lease vocabulary, bounded failure, redaction, compatibility, and explicit unsupported behavior.
10. **G10 bounded failure:** all-exhausted and resident-unavailable cases end once with a typed outcome and trusted `Retry-After`, without loops, invented capacity, or restart.
11. **G11 beta cohort:** three clean non-maintainer users, including one Linux user, complete install, enrollment, managed launch, handoff, repair, and rollback on the exact candidate.

## Trigger and claim boundary

The live G1/G8 trigger is provider-originated quota exhaustion. Pre-body 401/403 remain required synthetic negative coverage but do not substitute for the live continuity trigger. Stages 0-3 are prerequisites and earn no row. Stage 4 installed/service dogfood remains blocked until TIN-1759 is Done with accepted proof and the ladder's O-OWNERSHIP and R-TIN-1759 gates are accepted. v0.1.15 stays the stable shipped release until promotion is explicitly accepted.

after.description:
## Superseded by native reset — 2026-10-02

Removed legacy health.zig codec no longer belongs to fresh runtime; current typed/request boundaries replace integrity work.

Replacement: [TIN-1798](https://linear.app/tinyland/issue/TIN-1798). This is cancellation of an incompatible proposal, not completion or deletion of its history. [Active reset](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/plans/omux-native-account-lifecycle-reset-2026-10-02.md>) governs new work. Historical v0.1.15 evidence retains its exact claim boundary.

## Preserved historical proposal

## Problem

TIN-3006 review found a broader pre-existing invariant gap outside its three-file charter.

`src/health.zig` encodes route state into a fixed 256-byte `provider:account#capability` key. `KeyBuf.append` silently truncates, and `parseHealthKey` interprets the first `#` after the provider/account separator as the capability boundary. Current config validation rejects `:` in provider names but does not reject `#` in account/capability names or prove that every configured account/capability key fits losslessly.

That permits two configured routes to collide or become unparseable in persisted health state. TIN-3006 fails closed at its new planning front doors, but it must not expand into shared config/health ownership.

## Scope

* Define one lossless health-key constructor/validator shared by config and runtime users.
* Reject reserved separators in account and capability names at config validation.
* Reject any configured account or capability route whose encoded key exceeds the codec limit; do not truncate.
* Cover custom provider definitions as well as built-ins.
* Preserve valid colon-containing account labels if the codec/parser contract intentionally supports them.
* Audit all direct `accountKey`/`capabilityKey` callers for silent-truncation assumptions.

## Acceptance

* Config validation fails with field-specific errors for `#` collisions and overlong account/capability routes.
* Property/boundary tests prove encode/parse round-trip and uniqueness for all accepted keys.
* No runtime health path can create a truncated key.
* Existing valid config and emitted compatibility bytes remain unchanged.
* Exact-head GF Test and GF Check pass.

## Claim boundary

This is route-state integrity hardening. It does not move Stage 4, G11, or TIN-2057 and does not authorize credential/provider access.

after.title: Claude managed adapter: authenticated per-session ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL request proxy
after.description:
## Superseded by native reset — 2026-10-02

Managed omux claude launcher as required entrypoint and optional resident sidecar policy are superseded. Claude native ordinary-launch gate owns follow-on.

Replacement: [TIN-2077](https://linear.app/tinyland/issue/TIN-2077). This is cancellation of an incompatible proposal, not completion or deletion of its history. [Active reset](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/plans/omux-native-account-lifecycle-reset-2026-10-02.md>) governs new work. Historical v0.1.15 evidence retains its exact claim boundary.

## Preserved historical proposal

## Outcome

Implement the v0.2 managed Claude adapter as a per-session authenticated loopback request proxy. `omux claude [-- <args>]` launches Claude Code with an ephemeral `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and a base64url 256-bit capability in `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`. Bare `claude` is untouched.

## Contract

* Bind loopback only; keep the capability memory-only, compare in constant time, strip it upstream, and return local 401 with zero upstream calls on mismatch. An instrumented launch must prove Claude Code's bearer carrier before claiming this boundary.
* Forward origin-form requests only to compile-fixed `https://api.anthropic.com`; reject CONNECT, absolute-form, arbitrary destinations, caller-selected upstreams, and credential-carrying redirects.
* Strip inbound auth/API-key headers and inject only the elected account's OAuth credential.
* Preserve the exact requested model.
* Permit one cross-account alternate only for explicit pre-body 401/403/429. Provider 5xx passes through. Never replay started responses or ambiguous transport outcomes.
* Replay budgets are 32 MiB/request, 64 MiB/sidecar, and 256 MiB/host with atomic reservations/stale-PID cleanup. Budget or chunked overflow becomes stream-once; no disk spooling.
* Refresh at request boundary through the existing per-account flock. Hard rotating-refresh-token failure quarantines the route and requires provider-owned re-enrollment; never restore stale token backups.
* When all routes are exhausted, wait once only for a trusted reset within 30 seconds and the request deadline, then typed 429 plus Retry-After.
* The resident service remains refresh/observation/alert/snapshot only, never the request proxy.

## First proof

A deterministic fake Anthropic upstream proves carrier behavior, bad-token zero-call rejection, fixed-origin/redirect negatives, streaming pass-through, exact-model preservation, single-alternate 401/403/429, 5xx pass-through, ambiguous/started exclusions, replay budgets, cleanup, and redaction. Live proof follows under TIN-2077.

## Superseded by native reset — 2026-10-02

Removed claudeKeychainService derivation is predecessor-specific; authorized source/OS vault contract replaces native-store intent.

Replacement: [TIN-2078](https://linear.app/tinyland/issue/TIN-2078). This is cancellation of an incompatible proposal, not completion or deletion of its history. [Active reset](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/plans/omux-native-account-lifecycle-reset-2026-10-02.md>) governs new work. Historical v0.1.15 evidence retains its exact claim boundary.

## Preserved historical proposal

Surfaced by the TIN-2054-#2 review (confirmed latent, pre-existing — not introduced by the guard).

`provider_schema.claudeKeychainService` ALWAYS appends a `-<sha256(dir)[:8]>` suffix, yet its own doc-comment (and the TIN-2060 proof) states the default dir `~/.claude` uses the **unsuffixed base** `Claude Code-credentials` (the service bare Claude Code uses when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is unset). So:

* A managed Claude account configured with `config_dir: "~/.claude"` (or `$HOME/.claude`) and `service: null` derives `Claude Code-credentials-<hash(~/.claude)>` — the **wrong** service. The real item for that dir is (per the bare-CLI contract) the unsuffixed base, so oauth-mux would **read/write a non-existent/foreign keychain item** → the account is broken at the read layer before refresh ever runs.
* The TIN-2054-#2 canonical-keychain guard (exact-match on the unsuffixed base) therefore CANNOT catch this suffixed-but-wrong form. It only protects the literal base-string form (what `omux init` produces, and what the live `personal` account uses). The `~/.claude`-as-config_dir case is independently malfunctioning, so practical revoke-risk is low — but the comment-vs-code contradiction is a real latent defect.

**Root unknown (TIN-2060):** does the Claude CLI use the suffixed or the base service when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is exported AND equals the default `~/.claude`? Resolve it, then:

* **(a)** special-case `claudeKeychainService` to return the unsuffixed base when the absolute dir equals the resolved `~/.claude` (so the derived service matches the CLI's, and the canonical guard's exact-match correctly catches the only true bare-Claude form); OR
* **(b)** document that `~/.claude` is unsupported as a managed `config_dir` and refuse it at config-load (the cleaner posture, since a managed account should never share the bare-Claude item — and the live `personal` account, which IS `~/.claude`, should perhaps be modeled as "the user's own Claude, not mux-managed for refresh").

**Acceptance:** the derived keychain service for a `~/.claude` config_dir matches whatever the live CLI actually uses (golden-vector verified), OR `~/.claude` is explicitly refused as a managed config_dir with a clear message. Connects to TIN-2078 (declarable os-keystore).

after.title: Retention: bound status ndjson / smoke dirs; opt-in per-account sessions sweep
after.description:
## Superseded by native reset — 2026-10-02

Removed managed status directories and per-account-home session sweep conflict with preserved native stores; fresh redacted state owns bounded metadata.

Replacement: [TIN-1803](https://linear.app/tinyland/issue/TIN-1803). This is cancellation of an incompatible proposal, not completion or deletion of its history. [Active reset](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/plans/omux-native-account-lifecycle-reset-2026-10-02.md>) governs new work. Historical v0.1.15 evidence retains its exact claim boundary.

## Preserved historical proposal

Unbounded state growth: every managed run writes `state/codex/status/managed-<ts>.ndjson` (483 files observed; up to 525KB each); smoke commands leave `codex-broker-*-smoke-<ts>` dirs; `latestCodexStatusPath` stat-sweeps the whole dir per `codex status` (`src/main.zig:11087-11113`). Per-account homes also accumulate `sessions/` rollouts with no sweep (acknowledged TIN-1851 follow-up).

**In scope**: keep-last-N (configurable) prune of status files + smoke dirs at session start; bounded, opt-in `sessions/` retention sweep per account home (default: keep everything until explicitly enabled — sessions are user data).

**Out of scope**: canonical \~/.codex (never ours to prune).

**Acceptance**: status dir bounded after N runs; sessions sweep refuses to run without explicit config/flag; sweep never touches a home whose account lock is held.

## Problem

Lighthouse a11y audit (2026-04-30, 97/100 desktop+mobile) flags 15 elements with WCAG AA color-contrast under threshold:

1. `chip preset-filled-success-500` / `preset-filled-warning-500` / `preset-filled-error-500` — chip text on filled coloured backgrounds. The Skeleton 4 default text colour for these presets is borderline against the OKLCH theme's primary/warning/error fills.
2. `text-surface-500` on `figure` background in `LivenessLadder.svelte` — the `#1`/`#2`/`#3` row indicators sit at mid-gray on the warm cream backdrop, dropping below the 4.5:1 ratio at 12px.

## Acceptance

* All chip presets pass WCAG AA at the 4.5:1 ratio for normal text. Likely fix: bump chip text colour from default to `text-{scale}-contrast-700-300` or similar Skeleton 4 contrast token.
* LivenessLadder row indicators bumped from `text-surface-500` to `text-surface-600-400`.
* Re-run Lighthouse, target a11y 100/100.

## Source

`docs/launch/post-launch-verification-2026-04-30.md` § Specific Lighthouse audits failing.

after.title: Design multi-account OAuth muxing for agent and connector auth
after.description:
## Problem

The current AI lab auth persistence path assumes one active OAuth identity per tool/provider. That is too narrow. OpenAI alone has likely work and personal accounts, and similar multi-account/session ambiguity exists for FlakeHub and other browser/device-code OAuth providers.

We need a deliberate architecture sprint for muxing multiple OAuth identities and sessions across repo-managed agent harnesses without guessing or overwriting the wrong account.

## Scope

* Inventory OAuth-backed providers and tools currently in play: OpenAI/Codex/OpenCode, FlakeHub/Determinate, Vercel if applicable, GitHub connector/plugin auth, Linear connector/OAuth, Figma, Claude, and any other browser/device-code auth flows.
* Define an account/session naming model that can distinguish work vs personal vs service/operator identities.
* Decide where account selection lives: repo config, host config, user-local mutable state, wrapper flags, environment variables, or interactive selection.
* Define safe SOPS/age persistence for multi-account OAuth stores without committing plaintext tokens or collapsing distinct accounts into one file.
* Define verification surfaces that can prove which account/session a tool is using without printing token values.
* Define migration behavior for existing single-account auth stores.

## Non-goals

* Do not opportunistically patch OpenCode only.
* Do not assume one default identity is globally correct.
* Do not store raw OAuth tokens in shell env or `.env` files.
* Do not claim model/provider parity if account selection is ambiguous.

## Acceptance criteria

* Architecture/runbook describes the provider inventory, account identity model, persistence layout, selection mechanism, and verification commands.
* Repo validation can report configured account labels and active selected account per tool where the upstream tool exposes enough metadata.
* Home Manager/SOPS design supports at least OpenAI work/personal account separation without overwriting the active local OAuth store accidentally.
* GitHub issue #197 is linked for implementation tracking.

## Existing substrate and historical scope

I-54 and six active projects are reused, not duplicated. Both canceled federation/C ABI projects remain canceled; Done tickets and TIN-491 remain intact. Twenty-four active compatible tickets now carry native scope plus their full predecessor descriptions. Seven incompatible proposals were canceled with replacement links, not deleted. TIN-824 remains website accessibility work.

Historical TIN-2057 0/11 / 82-pass / 42-missing scores remain in its preserved appendix for their exact July candidate. They are not successor proof. v0.1.15 remains historical stable release; new reset remains experimental and unshipped.

From 2026-10-02 23:41:49 EDT / 2026-10-03T03:41:49Z: +3h Oct3 02:41:49 EDT; +5h Oct3 04:41:49 EDT; +10h Oct3 09:41:49 EDT; weekend Oct4 23:59 EDT. [Weekend plan](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/plans/omux-ratification-weekend-push-2026-10-02.md>).

## Reliability and resources

REL numeric objectives are adopted measurement targets, unmeasured. Current experimental software has no contractual SLA, service credits, staffed support or human on-call. Severity S0–S3 informs backlog triage only; future agreement response times are proposed terms.

Local source/fixture proof cannot close upstream native availability, ordinary launch/resume/attachment, live compatible handoff, actual Secret Service/Keychain, installed services/desktops, macOS SDK/platform, refresh owner adoption or production browser schemas. Each is an explicit issue dependency/resource gate. Browser acquisition is optional and production exports stay disabled pending proof. Omux ships no Codex fork.

oauth-mux owns runtime/API/capability/release evidence. Official Codex owns native hook acceptance. [omux.xoxd.ai](<http://omux.xoxd.ai>) owns rendering and exact generated bundle imports, never runtime claims. Homebrew consumes published release facts; infrastructure/operator credentials remain outside source. No GitHub posts, deployment, tap/provider mutation or publication occurred here.

All executable validation/generation/packaging uses locked Nix plus Bazel/Bazelisk, locally by default; no automatic CI, Just or GF requirement. Exact mutation receipts live in docs/tracker-updates/native-ratification-2026-10-02.{md,json}.
